title: Technical Sector Officer - Livestock, AIM (Kisii/Kakamega)
description:
Location: Kisii,Kisii County,Kenya

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organization, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 16 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit (www.bracinternational.org)

About the AIM Program
The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway.

About the AIM Education Pathway
The AIM Education pathway is designed to increase access to and completion of quality secondary education for adolescent girls, aged 12-17, across the AIM countries: Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to support adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to improve gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students.
This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better prepare young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community support, and weak school governance systems.

JOB SUMMARY
The role of Technical Sector Officer, Livestock (TSO-L) will provide hands on support to the Technical Coordinator and Regional Manager - AIM to ensure all livestock and TVET with related market development activities, including implementation of livelihoods, market development and market facilitation activities, are effectively delivered and on time. This role will also provide support to develop and contextualize asset-specific training modules; train frontline staff on the newly developed training materials; help develop the detailed participant training rollout plans and support the cascading down of the training. The role will also support the operations team in budgeting, in ensuring quality procurement, asset distribution and asset management support.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Technical Sector Support

  • Support the planning and delivery of livelihood activities in livestock and poultry; including training, asset procurement and transfer, asset follow-up, facilitating linkages with market actors and service providers.
  • Provide support to the Technical Coordinators for the development of specific livelihood pathways training modules, as needed.
  • Support the training of front line staff on the newly developed training materials; finalize the participant training rollout plans and provide logistics and planning support to the cascading down of the training.
  • Support the budgeting, planning and delivery of all livestock related livelihood interventions, including supporting localized market assessments; training on chosen livelihood pathways and entrepreneurship; asset mapping, procurement, distribution and management.
  • Support the facilitation of relevant linkages to small business , apprenticeship and entrepreneurship.
  • Support the training of branch staff and ensure the participant's economic needs assessment/economic profiling and market assessments are done effectively prior to livelihood selection.
  • Support the selection and training of the Community Livestock Promoter and ensure they are ready to provide service to participants.
  • Be informed of and compile a full list of national laws and regulations (such as quarantine requirements for livestock), disseminate this knowledge with field teams and ensure all livelihoods and market development interventions are developed in accordance with the existing laws.
  • Perform periodic review of training modules and make necessary changes, as needed in joint collaboration with the Technical Coordinator - LMD.
  • Support the Technical Coordinator - GESI for to effectively integrate GESI considerations in program activities, including making accommodations for vulnerable groups such as PWDs, IDP, refugees, and other relevant underrepresented groups.

Coordination and Planning Support

  • Support communication with key stakeholders (government and non-government) and collect relevant training materials that can be used to develop/strengthen/ contextualize BRAC’s training materials.
  • Support coordination with a range of stakeholders, including government entities, INGOs, CSOs, YDC members, service providers, to support delivery of interventions.

Reporting Support

  • Regularly check MIS and ensure proper reporting, data accuracy and validation

Safeguarding

  • Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the project goals on safeguarding implementation.
  • Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
  • Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.


EXPERIENCE

  • 3 years of relevant experience, preferring in programs focused on livelihoods or economic development
  • Previous experience in providing technical assistance, especially related to livelihood or economic empowerment related activities, training module development, and training facilitation
  • Previous experience working in integrated programs targeted for women is a plus.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & COMPETENCIES (required to perform all the responsibilities of this role):

  • Training materials development and staff capacity development
  • Computer literacy
  • Report writing
  • Degree-DVM /Animal husbandry or any other related subject.

HOW TO APPLY

This is an outstanding opportunity to work with BRAC International. If you feel you are the right match
for the position mentioned above, please follow the application instructions accordingly:
Please submit your resume, including all job assignments in detail, and cover letter via the
below link :Technical Sector Officer - Livestock, AIM
Only complete applications will be accepted, and short-listed candidates will be contacted.
Application deadline: 9th October 2026.

We believe every stakeholder and every member of the communities we work with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm, abuse, neglect, harassment, and exploitation -regardless of age, race, religion, and gender, status as an individual with a disability or ethnic origin.   • £1000 refer a friend bonus
  • Annual performance-related pay increases
  • Brilliant career progression opportunities
  • Company awards, celebrations and team social events
  • Access to a healthcare cash plan
  • Early access to pay through the Hastee app
  • Perkbox discounts and savings on thousands of retailers

We are looking for an Early Years Apprentice to join our team at Kido Imperial Wharf, St Michaels Centre, Townmead Rd, London SW6 2SR.

  • Your values will align with our 3 core values - Listen, Learn and Lead

  • Collaborate with a supportive team to deliver exceptional childcare, nursery events, and enriching learning experiences.
  • Benefit from ongoing professional development opportunities while building a rewarding career in early years education.


What’s next?

If you’re ready to seize the opportunity to join the Kido team and build a fulfilling career apply today and we’ll be in touch. You can expect an initial phone call with one of our Talent Partners who will take you through the next stages.

If you have any questions don’t hesitate to reach out to us via careers@kido.school


Safer Recruitment

All posts involving direct contact with children are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. However, amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975 (2013 & 2020) provide that certain spent convictions and cautions are 'protected'. These are not subject to disclosure to employers and cannot be taken into account. Guidance and criteria on the filtering of these cautions and convictions can be found on the Ministry of Justice website or see here.

Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide details of all unspent convictions and those that would not be filtered, prior to the date of the interview. You may be asked for further information about your criminal history during the recruitment process. If your application is successful, this self-disclosure information will be checked against information from the Disclosure & Barring Service before your appointment is confirmed.

*If you are unsure whether you need to disclose criminal information, you should seek legal advice or you may wish to contact Nacro or Unlock for impartial advice. There is more information on filtering and protected offences on the Ministry of Justice website.

title: OHL Draughting Technical Lead

title: Logistics Site Coordinator
description:
Overview

Logistics Site Coordinator Energy Valley Project - Minya

At Scatec, you get to work on something that matters. We develop, build, own, and operate renewable energy solutions that accelerate access to reliable and affordable clean energy. As part of a global and agile organisation, you will work with skilled colleagues across functions and geographies, take real ownership, and contribute to a company driven by the vision of improving our future. At the heart of everything we do is our belief that we bring the energy - the energy for change, connection, and growth. It shapes how we collaborate, innovate, and create impact together. If you are looking for a role where your contribution is visible, your development matters, and your work supports a more sustainable future, Scatec may be the right place for you.

Ready to make an impact?

Why this role matters

The Logistics Site Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring the efficient flow, control, and availability of materials required for project execution. By maintaining accurate inventory records, coordinating material deliveries and issuance, and supporting logistics operations across the project site, this role helps ensure uninterrupted construction activities, compliance with project requirements, and effective cost control throughout the project lifecycle.

What you'll be doing

In this role, you will:

  • Coordinate the receipt, inspection, and documentation of materials, equipment, and containers arriving at the project site.
  • Prepare and maintain Material Receipt Notes (MRNs), Material Issue Notes (MINs), and all supporting logistics documentation.
  • Maintain accurate inventory records, material tracking logs, and stock reconciliation activities across the project site.
  • Monitor material issuance, consumption, transfers, returns, and storage locations to ensure visibility and accountability.
  • Coordinate deliveries and transportation activities with suppliers, contractors, warehouses, and project stakeholders.
  • Support construction teams by providing material status updates, inventory reports, and shortage or surplus alerts.
  • Prepare logistics, inventory, transportation, and material control reports for project management and supply chain teams.
  • Ensure compliance with company procedures, quality standards, documentation requirements, and HSE regulations across all logistics activities.

Your work will support real decisions, real assets, and real operational outcomes.

What you'll gain

  • Professional growth through ownership, exposure, and meaningful contribution from day one.
  • Hands-on experience in a role where the challenge is energising, fast-moving, meaningful, and built on learning through doing.
  • Exposure to large-scale renewable energy construction projects and international supply chain operations.
  • Opportunity to work closely with project, construction, procurement, warehouse, and logistics teams across multiple functions.

What you'll bring

Experience and qualifications

  • 2 to 5 years of experience in logistics, warehouse operations, inventory control, material management, or site coordination.
  • Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Experience managing material receipt, issuance, inventory tracking, and stock reconciliation processes on construction or industrial projects.
  • Strong knowledge of logistics documentation, delivery records, transportation coordination, and inventory control systems.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, and experience using ERP or inventory management systems.
  • Fluent in English, spoken and written.

    What it’s like to work at Scatec

    At Scatec, we combine purpose with performance. We value responsibility, clarity, and collaboration and we encourage people to challenge existing ways of working, contribute ideas, and keep developing. You can expect an environment where people work together across disciplines and geographies, where good performance matters, and where you are trusted to take ownership without unnecessary hierarchy.

    If you are motivated by analysis with purpose, commercial insight, and real operational impact, this could be a strong next step in your career.

    What we offer

    At Scatec, you will be part of a company with a clear and ambitious purpose, working on renewable energy solutions that make a lasting difference. You will gain responsibility early, learn from experienced colleagues, and build your capabilities in a business that offers global exposure, strong development opportunities, and meaningful work in the energy transition. We are continuously evolving as a digital and data-driven organisation, leveraging technology and AI to improve how we work and create value for our teams

    Scatec is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment based on merit, competence, and business needs.

    We review applications on an ongoing basis.

title: Learning Technologist (SEND)
description:
Learning Technologist (SEND)

Hours; Full time (37 hours each week, all year-round)

Duration; Permanent

Salary; £32,515 a year + benefits

Location; Working across all RNN Group sites in Rotherham and Worksop

Apply by; 12/10/2026

About the Role

In the 2026 educational landscape, technology is the ultimate tool for equity. We believe that when we design for accessibility, we improve the learning experience for everyone. To ensure our high-tech innovations leave no one behind, we are seeking a passionate, tech-savvy Assistive Technology Specialist to champion the success of our SEND learners.

As the Learning Technology specialising in SEND, you will act as the "Ethical Compass" and "Accessibility Lead" for the Digital Innovation & AI department. Reporting directly to the Digital Learning Manager, you will ensure that the college's digital ecosystem—from AI-driven speech-to-text to immersive sensory environments—is inclusive by default, not by exception.

You are more than a technical expert; you are a coach, an advisor, and a lead advocate for inclusive practice. While others focus on how to teach or how content looks, your focus is entirely on how it is accessed. You will work at the heart of the curriculum to ensure that "Reasonable Adjustments" are transformed from administrative paperwork into active, empowering digital realities.

In 2026, the primary challenge lies in keeping pace with the rapid, weekly evolution of AI-powered assistive tools; constantly researching and vetting new software to ensure it is safe, effective, and compatible. Additionally, you will champion the culture of "Inclusion by Design," navigating the human challenge of convincing time-poor curriculum teams to build accessibility into their resources from the very beginning, rather than as an afterthought.

Key Responsibilities

  • Specialist Learner Support: Provide direct, hands-on support to SEND learners, equipping themwith the personalised digital toolkits they need to access the curriculum with confidence and independence.
  • Staff Inclusion Training: Design and deliver specialised training for teaching and support staff, empowering them to embed inclusive digital practices into daily lessons.
  • Accessibility Consultancy: Advise the department and the wider college on WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) compliance, ensuring all digital platforms and resources are legally and ethically accessible.
  • Barrier Removal & Auditing: Proactively audit curriculum materials to identify and eliminate digital "blockers," adapting learning materials to meet the needs of diverse student cohorts.
  • Reasonable Adjustments: Lead the classroom implementation of digital reasonable adjustments, leveraging technology to level the playing field for assessments and activities.
  • Policy Contribution: Contribute to the development of inclusive digital policies, ensuring SEND requirements remain at the forefront of the Group’s over-arching AI and Digital Strategy.
  • Intervention & Escalation: Act as a critical link between students and academic teams, escalating complex accessibility or technical framework issues to senior staff for swift resolution.

Key Role Objectives

  • Learner Independence: Measurably increase the ability of SEND students to work and study independently through the mastery of assistive software and hardware.
  • Institutional Compliance: Ensure 100% of the Group’s primary digital learning resources meet or exceed current WCAG accessibility standards.
  • Capability Building: Raise the institutional baseline of inclusive teaching, ensuring all faculty members can confidently use standard assistive tools within the VLE.

You will…

  • We are looking for a compassionate, resilient, and highly organised professional who believes that accessibility is a fundamental right.
  • SEND & Assistive Tech Expertise: Proven experience working with SEND learners and a deep technical understanding of assistive software, hardware, and emerging AI accessibility tools.
  • Accessibility Standards: Strong working knowledge of WCAG compliance and digital inclusion best practices.
  • Educational Background: Experience working within an FE/HE, training provider, or alternative provision environment.
  • Collaborative Communicator: Ability to build strong partnerships with the Quality Team, IT technicians, and SEND Leads to bridge the gap between infrastructure and individual learner needs.
  • Cultural Influencer: Excellent coaching and advocacy skills, with the resilience needed to drive cultural and pedagogical change across diverse staff teams.
  • You will hold a Level 2 (or equivalent) qualification in English and Maths (or be willing to undertake) and a degree level (or equivalent) qualification in special education, digital accessibility or IT as well as a specialist certification in assistive technologies or digital accessibility would be desirable.

We understand that no candidate will perfectly match every qualification or criterion listed. If your experience differs from what we've outlined but you believe you can contribute to this role, we encourage you to apply!

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for RNN Group, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Prime
description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Prime team's mission is to build Bitstamp's prime brokerage for institutional clients — the platform that lets hedge funds, market makers, and professional trading firms onboard, fund, trade, borrow against, and settle positions at scale. We build the systems that move real institutional money: cross-venue settlement, credit against collateral, matched-book lending, and the bridge that brings tokenized securities to our order book — together with the client- and ops-facing surfaces that make them usable, from institutional onboarding and account configuration to reporting and the backoffice tooling our operations run on every day. These are correctness-critical systems where a wrong answer can't be cheaply undone — getting them right is the whole job.

As a Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer, you will own the design and end-to-end delivery of features across that whole surface — from the Prime backend services down to the frontend and backoffice screens that expose them. You'll lead other engineers through problems of high ambiguity, set the technical bar for how we build for failure and not just the happy path, and follow a problem across the full institutional lifecycle rather than stopping at a boundary. Flexibility is the job: some weeks that's a settlement edge case in the backend, others a client onboarding flow or an ops dashboard, and you're happy owning whichever the work needs.

This role is based in our Ljubljana, Slovenia office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

Applications for this role will be accepted through October 30, 2026.

Requires participation in an on-call rotation to support business needs.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the design and end-to-end delivery of features across the stack — from Prime backend services (settlement, on-exchange credit, lending, tokenized securities) through to the frontend and backoffice screens clients and ops teams rely on.

  • Own the client- and ops-facing journeys across the institutional lifecycle — onboarding, account configuration, reporting, and the tooling that lets operations run the business safely.

  • Author detailed designs and break work into reviewable steps, making failure states, invariants, and recovery explicit before you ship — on flows where a wrong answer moves real money.

  • Uplevel the team through design-focused code review and mentorship, and move fluidly between backend and frontend as the work demands rather than handing off at a boundary.

What you bring

  • A track record of independently delivering complex, high-ambiguity projects with long-term impact, operating them in production and owning every line you ship.

  • Strong full-stack range in production — a modern backend (we work primarily in Python/Django and Go) and a component-based frontend (we use Vue) — with the judgment to know where a given problem is best solved and a genuine willingness to own whatever the feature needs, wherever it lives in the stack.

  • Hands-on experience building financial systems — user balances, ledgers, risk engines, settlement, onboarding/KYC, or payments — where correctness is non-negotiable and mistakes are expensive.

  • Strong design judgment: you enumerate the failure paths, name your invariants, and can point at the constraint, test, or alert that enforces each one.

  • Excellent communication: you drive alignment across teams and stakeholders, give substantive design-level review feedback, and mentor engineers to raise the bar around you.

🎁 What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career and build cutting-edge financial infrastructure.

title: Senior Officer - IT, AIM (Kisii/Kakamega)
description:
Location: Kisii,Kisii County,Kenya

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organization, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 16 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit (www.bracinternational.org)

About the AIM Program
The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway.

About the AIM Education Pathway
The AIM Education pathway is designed to increase access to and completion of quality secondary education for adolescent girls, aged 12-17, across the AIM countries: Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to support adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to improve gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students.
This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better prepare young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community support, and weak school governance systems.

JOB SUMMARY
The Senior Officer, IT will be responsible for providing comprehensive IT support to the Regional Office(s) and branches within the assigned region(s). The position will provide first-level support for hardware, end-user devices, software, internet and network connectivity, and business applications used by the Regional Office, branches, and programme teams. The role will ensure timely issue resolution, user support, and documentation in line with BI Technology standards.

  • Coordinate with the Senior Manager, IT to log, monitor, and resolve user issues efficiently.
  • Triage complex technical issues that cannot be resolved on-site and escalate them to the appropriate internal teams (e.g. HO IT, product management, program) with detailed documentation and a clear root-cause analysis through Jira.
  • Ensure stable and secure connectivity across all offices by managing routers, switches, and wireless access points. Diagnose and resolve network issues promptly.
  • Install, configure, and maintain laptops, desktops, printers, scanners, and other IT equipment. Provide timely technical support to end-users and assist in implementing endpoint protection, antivirus, and patch management solutions.
  • Build and maintain strong, positive relationships with end users by understanding their business needs, managing their expectations, and providing exceptional service.
  • Act as the primary liaison between the field, program and the Country IT team, ensuring seamless communication and alignment on technology initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate and timely records of all support activities, including technical issues, resolutions, and client communication, in our ticketing and knowledge base systems.
  • Provide in-person training and support to end-users on application usage and best practices. Assist with the technical onboarding of new employees or clients at their location.
  • Establish and enforce IT policies, procedures, and best practices to ensure compliance with global standards and regulatory requirements.

EXPERIENCE

  • Experience working in international NGO/development sector will be highly preferred.

Job Description

In this role, you will combine strategy with execution. You will help to put our proposition on the map, motivate customers, lead projects, and build your own Software Engineering team. You are both a visionary and a doer, from architecture and code reviews to implementation and deployment.

Your role

  • You will take responsibility for building and expanding the software development team within adesso Belgium, support new customer acquisition, actively share knowledge within the team, and contribute to team growth.

    • You design and implement cloud‑native applications with C#, the .NET framework, and Azure Cloud Services, ensuring stable and secure integration with other systems.

    • You develop front‑end components in Blazor (or any JavaScript/TypeScript framework such as React, Angular or Vue) that connect to backend services and contribute to an optimal user experience.

  • You work closely with developers, designers, and architects, take responsibility for the final delivery quality, and ensure the optimal balance between customer requirements and resources.
  • As we grow, you will mentor and lead new team members. Your people skills will enable you to train junior consultants and coordinate their work. You'll foster a positive team environment, provide guidance, and eventually manage the Software team, helping each member develop their skills.
  • You build a local community and take the lead in our internal and international AI community ‘new school of AI’ for Belgium; you generate knowledge, experience and best practices that you can share within this community and use in your business plan around this specific topic.
  • More info around the new school of AI: https://www.adesso.de/en/impulse/new-school-of-ai/index.jsp

Required Skills & Knowledge

C#, .NET Framework (10+ and ASP.NET Core), Azure Cloud Services, including App Services, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, and Key Vault. Entity Framework Core, Docker, Kubernetes (AKS).

Your profile

  • You have a strong passion for building high‑quality digital solutions and the ability to convince both customers and colleagues.
  • You have an extensive experience in C# and the .NET Framework (10+ and ASP.NET Core) and with Azure Cloud Services, including App Services, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, and Key Vault.
  • You have knowledge of modern software architectures (microservices, event‑driven, cloud‑native).
  • Proficiency with CI/CD, version control (Git), test automation, and monitoring tools.
  • You have led multiple large software implementations successfully. From planning and design to deployment, you have been responsible for delivering complex projects, possibly in a consulting or integrator environment.
  • You possess experience in presales and customer‑facing engagements. You are comfortable running discovery sessions, preparing demos or prototypes, and you can convincingly articulate the business value of proposed solutions. RFPs, demo presentations, and crafting solution proposals are part of your skillset.
  • You possess excellent people and communication skills. You can manage stakeholders at all levels and build trustful relationships with clients. Internally, you are a natural leader and mentor – capable of onboarding new team members, sharing knowledge, and guiding colleagues to success.
  • You have completed a bachelor's or master's degree in Software Engineering or a related field, along with at least 7 years of relevant professional or project experience.
  • Experience in a lead or senior role, with proven success in guiding teams and projects.
  • You are trilingual in Dutch, French, and English.

Why join adesso Belgium?

  • Meaningful work and projects: work within your domain of expertise where you can create value for customers and grow together with the company.
  • Strategic opinion: your opinion and contribution to the expansion of the company is very valuable and counts! You can give the company direction bringing in your ideas, creativity and vision for future growth!
  • GrowTogether: with over 400 training courses and our digital learning platform, we support your continuous development.
  • Knowledge sharing & building communities: you will build a knowledge center and software engineering community – our plan is to build an adesso community of 70 co‑workers in December 2027!
  • Work‑Life Balance & Flexibility: Enjoy hybrid working options and a dynamic work environment. We are located near the Brussels North Train Station in “Gare Maritime – Tour & Taxi” where a variety of facilities, such as a food corner, gym, padel courts, …, and even a skate park are available.
  • Comprehensive benefits: Competitive salary, company car with mobility budget, charging card, net allowance, meal vouchers, insurances and 32 days of annual leave.
  • Global reach with local expertise: you will be part of a small agile company where our culture code will drive us to success. As part of an international company we are supported in different domains with expertise and top‑notch reference cases!

title: Refrigeration Engineer
description:
Refrigeration Engineer

Location: London - M25
Main Areas: West End & East London
Salary: £55,000 basic + Company Vehicle + Fuel Card + Benefits
Employment: Full-Time, Permanent

We are looking for an experienced Refrigeration Engineer with strong hands-on experience working with cold rooms, commercial fridges and refrigeration systems to join a growing specialist team covering London and the M25.

This is an excellent opportunity for an engineer who wants a long-term career with a specialist refrigeration company, where technical ability, customer service and quality workmanship are genuinely valued.

You will primarily be working across Central London, the West End and East London, carrying out planned preventative maintenance, servicing, fault finding, repairs, commissioning and installation works on a variety of commercial refrigeration equipment.

The role offers a £55,000 basic salary, company vehicle and fuel card, with excellent overtime opportunities and a strong benefits package.

As a Refrigeration Engineer, you will be responsible for the servicing, maintenance, repair and installation of a range of commercial refrigeration equipment, with a particular focus on cold rooms, fridges and associated refrigeration systems.

Your duties will include, but are not limited to:

  • Routine servicing, maintenance and repairs of refrigeration systems
  • Mechanical and electrical fault finding and diagnostics
  • Working on commercial cold rooms, fridges and refrigeration equipment
  • Installation of refrigeration pipework and equipment
  • Refrigeration pipework brazing, bending, setting and joining
  • Pressure testing and brazing
  • Commissioning and servicing refrigeration systems
  • Refrigerant recovery
  • Leak testing, evacuation and refrigerant charging
  • Identifying faults and providing effective technical solutions
  • Carrying out preventative maintenance and ensuring equipment operates efficiently
  • Completing service reports and relevant documentation
  • Ensuring all work is completed to the highest possible standard
  • Maintaining excellent working relationships with customers and clients
  • Identifying potential new product or service opportunities
  • Working safely and in accordance with company procedures and legislation
  • Working independently and as part of a wider engineering team

There will also be occasional requirements for overnight stays away from home, with all reasonable business expenses covered by the company.

The Equipment

You will be working on a variety of commercial refrigeration systems and equipment, including:

  • Cold rooms
  • Commercial fridges
  • Refrigeration systems
  • Condensing units
  • Refrigeration pipework
  • Evaporators
  • Controls and associated electrical systems
  • Commercial refrigeration equipment

The successful candidate will be an experienced refrigeration professional with a strong background in the field and the ability to work confidently both independently and as part of a team.


You will ideally have:

  • F-Gas Category 1
  • NVQ Level 2/3 in Refrigeration & Air Conditioning - C&G 6187
  • Extensive practical experience within the refrigeration sector
  • Strong experience working on cold rooms and commercial refrigeration/fridges
  • Excellent refrigeration fault-finding and diagnostic skills

title: Deputy Program Manager - Federal Sector
location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description:
Procon is a top-ranked construction management and technology consulting firm with 25 years of experience delivering high‑impact projects across the U.S. and worldwide. An ENR Top 100 CM/PM firm for five consecutive years, we specialize in program management, project controls, commissioning, and technology—and offer an excellent platform to grow your career while shaping the future of the built environment.

Procon Consulting seeks an experienced Program Manager to support the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of Engraving & Printing (BEP), Facility Project Management Office (FPMO). The Program Manager will serve as the deputy and day-to-day strategic partner to the established Program Manager, supporting program leadership for BEP capital-facilities initiatives, including planning, programming, design, procurement, construction, transition, and related facility-project activities.

The ideal candidate brings demonstrated experience supporting programming, functional planning, and project-definition efforts for large, complex new-construction manufacturing, industrial, laboratory, mission-critical, or similarly operationally intensive facilities. The candidate also has substantial experience managing the design and construction of large buildings and coordinating multidisciplinary teams throughout the project lifecycle.

This position does not offer employment visa sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

Requirements

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, or a closely related discipline.
  • Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible experience managing large, complex capital projects or programs.
  • Senior leadership experience as a Deputy Program Manager, Senior Project Manager, Owner’s Representative, Construction Manager, or equivalent role.
  • Experience with programming, functional planning, needs assessments, and requirements development for complex manufacturing, industrial, production, laboratory, mission-critical, or similarly operational facilities.
  • Proven experience managing large-scale new construction involving complex MEP systems, specialized equipment, site infrastructure, security/access controls, high-reliability operations, and phased occupancy.
  • Ability to lead multiple interdependent workstreams and multidisciplinary teams within established program governance and delegated authority structures.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of preconstruction, design management, procurement, construction methods, cost management, scheduling, QA/QC, change management, commissioning, and closeout.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive briefings, reports, decision memoranda, meeting documentation, and stakeholder communications.
  • Experience developing and monitoring budgets, estimates, forecasts, cost variances, and financial reports; federal cost-estimating experience preferred.
  • Professional credentials such as PMP, CCM, PE, RA, DBIA, LEED AP, or comparable certifications preferred.
  • Federal, public-sector, institutional, industrial, manufacturing, or other highly regulated facility experience strongly preferred.

Responsibilities & Duties

  • Serve as the Program Manager’s principal deputy, providing day-to-day leadership for assigned capital projects and program workstreams from planning through construction, commissioning, occupancy, and closeout.
  • Manage project scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, stakeholder coordination, and overall delivery within delegated authority.
  • Represent the Program Manager in meetings, reviews, and coordination with BEP, federal partners, consultants, contractors, and other stakeholders as assigned.
  • Lead program workstreams involving requirements development, functional programming, project planning, design coordination, construction oversight, risk management, and transition planning.
  • Coordinate requirements for complex manufacturing and secure-production facilities, including workflows, utilities, equipment, security, logistics, adjacencies, and phasing.
  • Develop and maintain program management tools, including execution plans, integrated schedules, cost controls, risk registers, decision logs, action trackers, requirements-traceability tools, and reporting processes.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover activities across architectural, civil, structural, MEP, fire protection, utilities, security, technology, specialty systems, and FF&E disciplines.
  • Review design and construction deliverables, including drawings, estimates, schedules, constructability analyses, logistics and phasing plans, value-engineering proposals, submittals, shop drawings, and change documentation.
  • Lead executive briefings, design reviews, construction progress meetings, risk workshops, cost and schedule reviews, and stakeholder coordination sessions.
  • Monitor project performance against established scope, cost, schedule, quality, and risk objectives and develop mitigation strategies for emerging issues.
  • Oversee program-level estimating, budgeting, forecasting, funding tracking, progress measurement, and variance analysis.
  • Analyze integrated schedules using Microsoft Project, Primavera P6, or similar tools, including critical paths, milestones, long-lead procurement, permitting constraints, and recovery plans.
  • Support QA/QC through technical reviews, field observations, inspections, testing, commissioning, punch-list activities, and final closeout.
  • Prepare and quality-control executive dashboards, status reports, financial and schedule reports, risk summaries, decision papers, meeting records, presentations, and stakeholder communications.
  • Develop and implement program governance and standard operating procedures for document control, requirements management, design approvals, change control, project records, construction logistics, and closeout.

Physical Requirements

This position requires regular onsite presence in an active construction environment. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation, including:

  • Walking and standing for extended periods while performing site observations and inspections.

  • Navigating active construction areas, including stairs, uneven surfaces, temporary walkways, and varying elevations.

  • Occasionally bending, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and climbing as necessary to observe construction activities.

  • Accessing mechanical, electrical, utility, process, and other construction areas as required.

  • Wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE) and complying with all applicable site safety requirements.

  • Working in indoor and outdoor environments with exposure to typical construction-site conditions, including noise, dust, weather, and temperature fluctuations.

  • Occasionally lifting and carrying up to 25 pounds.

Benefits

Salary commensurate with experience.

Interested and qualified candidates please submit a cover letter and a resume.

Procon offers competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, including full medical/dental insurance and 401(K) plan. Procon is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, gender, age, color, religion, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other protected factor.

title: Sisältömarkkinoija / sisällöntuottaja (Content Marketer)
description:
**Freska**

Freska on kotisiivouspalvelu, joka on perustettu Suomessa vuonna 2015 – nykyään toimimme Suomessa, Ruotsissa ja Norjassa. Toimintaamme ohjaa yksi ajatus: onnelliset siivoojat = onnelliset asiakkaat. Freskalla työskentelee pohjoismaissa yli 1000 upeaa ammattisiivoojaa yli 50 eri maasta. Olemme rakentaneet kymmenen vuoden aikana ainutlaatuisia teknologiaratkaisuja, jotka mahdollistavat sujuvan ja modernin kokemuksen ja arjen niin asiakkaille kuin työntekijöillemme. Freska kasvaa hyvää vauhtia, joten nyt on oiva aika hypätä mukaan matkalle.

**Rooli**

Etsimme markkinointitiimiimme oma-aloitteista ja monipuolista sisällöntuottajaa, joka vie sisällön ideasta valmiiksi maksetun somen mainokseksi, orgaanisen somen sisällöksi, markkinointisähköpostiksi tai kampanjaländäriksi käden käänteessä ja laadulla. Käytössäsi on vahva brändi, kattavat sisältöpankkimme (brändiohjeistus, videot, kuvat, vaikuttaja- ja UGC-materiaalit), mutta tartut innokkaasti kameraan sekä mikkiin ja tuotat myös itse uutta materiaalia. Opit tuntemaan Freskan siivoojat – asiakkaidemme arjen sankarit, jotka antavat ihmisille aikaa ja vapautta – ja kerrot heidän tarinansa.

**Työtehtäväsi**

- Suunnittelet ja tuotat tuloksellista sisältöä sekä maksettuun mainontaan että orgaaniseen someen (Meta, Google ja TikTok), ideasta julkaisuun asti.

- Kirjoitat markkinointisähköposteja, jotka kiinnostavat ja tuottavat kauppaa.

- Työskentelet yhteistyössä tiimimme tuella ja ohjeistuksella kehittäen verkkosivujemme sisältöä – tavoitteena paras mahdollinen konversio, verkkosivukokemus sekä hakukone- ja tekoälylöydettävyys.

- Kuvaat uutta materiaalia omin kätösin: siivoojia, asiakkaita, koteja ja toimistoarkea – tarvittaessa astut itsekin kameran eteen ja se innostaa sinua.

- Osallistut sosiaalisen median vuorovaikutukseen vastaten sekä kommentteihin että yksityisviesteihin ruokkien parhaita mahdollisia kokemuksia brändimme ja ihmisten välillä.


**Mitä toivomme sinulta**

- Näyttöjä tuloksellisen sisällön tuottamisesta brändille, yritykselle tai vahvalle omalle kanavalle (näytä meille esimerkkejä).

- Kuvaat ja editoit videoita itsenäisesti ja varmalla otteella.

- Viihdyt kameran takana ja mieluiten myös sen edessä, kun sisältö sitä vaatii.

- Hyvä näppituntuma siihen, mikä somessa toimii ja trendaa juuri ja kyky kääntää tämä tuntuma toimiviksi sisällöiksi Freska-brändille.

- Olet oma-aloitteinen, järjestelmällinen ja otat mielelläsi palautetta vastaan.


**Mitä tarjoamme**

- Aloituspalkka noin 2800–3400 €/kk (riippuen kokemus- ja osaamistasostasi) sekä mahdollisuus kuukausittaiseen bonukseen, joka pohjautuu tuottamasi sisällön tuottamaan tilaajakannan ja liikevaihdon kasvuun.

- Kokoaikainen työsuhde ja rooli, jossa saat aidosti tukea ja mentorointia. Onnistumisesi, suoriutumisesi ja kehittymisesi ovat meille tärkeitä, joten esihenkilösi, lähin tiimisi ja koko organisaatio tukevat sinua aktiivisesti.

- Vastuuta ja vapautta suunnittelemasi ja luomasi sisällön suhteen.

- Nopeatempoinen, kansainvälinen tiimi, jossa pääset työskentelemnään monen eri alan osaajan kanssa – työkielenäsi käytät suomea sekä englantia .


**Näin haet**

Lähetä meille CV ja portfolio sisällöistä – mielellään sisältäen useita eri sisältötyyppejä. Toimi nopeasti, sillä käymme hakemuksia läpi jatkuvasti ja täytämme roolin heti sopivan henkilön löydyttyä.

title: Investor, Singapore (Software & AI Focus)
description:
About the firm

At January Capital, we invest in technology businesses that have a nexus to the Asia-Pacific region. We increasingly invest across a company's lifecycle and capital structure, but it all begins with data and our early stage investment focus. We manage more than $500 million on behalf of our investors, which include leading institutions, corporations, family offices, and high-net-worth individuals. Our portfolio includes Hupo, Akulaku, Shopback, Go1, Cyble, Tazapay, and others.


About the role

We are experiencing a period of growth across the firm. As we begin to deploy from our new venture fund series, we are searching for a driven, technically grounded investor to join (and potentially co-lead) our software investing team. This role will work closely with one of the firm’s Partners, supporting full lifecycle investing activities—from sourcing and diligence through to post-investment value creation.


The role is based in Singapore and will focus on investing in software and AI companies from the pre-seed stage, with a heavy index on evaluating founders, product, tech stacks and early market fit. This investor will also have the opportunity to dedicate 20-30% of their time towards building AI-native tooling and workflows for the firm, driving improvements in data-led investment decision making and portfolio management.


We are particularly interested in candidates who bring an entrepreneurial mindset, a strong technical background (AI/ML, data, infrastructure, software), and the ability to communicate their thinking clearly and insightfully. This hire will play a key role in strengthening the firm’s technical evaluation capabilities and expanding our network across the Asia-Pacific technical ecosystem.


Role responsibilities

  • Source and over time lead investments in early-stage software and AI/ML companies across Southeast Asia and other key Asia-Pacific markets.
  • Conduct technical and commercial diligence, including deep dives into product architecture, team background, early usage metrics, and go-to-market potential.
  • Contribute to thesis development in key software segments (e.g., developer tooling, SaaS infrastructure, applied AI in essential industries).
  • Develop internal AI-forward tools and workflows to support team decision-making and portfolio management processes.
  • Identify and engage with technical founders and academic/research talent across Southeast Asia, Australia, US and China.
  • Support portfolio companies post-investment on strategic initiatives, including product reviews, talent introductions, and customer access.
  • Contribute to firm-building activities (e.g., content, events, knowledge infrastructure).


What we’re looking for

  • A Bachelor’s or postgraduate degree in a technical field (Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Engineering, etc.) from a top-tier university in the US, Singapore, or equivalent. PhD or technical degrees are more than welcome.
  • 2–8+ years of experience in roles such as: (i) technical founder or early employee at a startup, (ii) software engineering or product roles at technology companies, (iii) research in AI/ML or applied data science, (iv) early-stage venture capital or investing roles with a technical bias
  • Interest in and ability to work confidently with cutting-edge AI tools and platforms, and serve as the subject matter expert for the investment team.
  • Demonstrated founder empathy—ideally through direct experience founding a company (successful or not), or having worked closely with founders.
  • You must demonstrate obsession with products and the AI/software ecosystem.
  • Proven ability to write, think, and communicate clearly – evidenced through writing samples, blog posts, or contributions to open-source projects.
  • A genuine curiosity in emerging technologies, products, and the people building them.
  • A willingness to roll up sleeves and work across sourcing, diligence, portfolio support, and internal initiatives.
  • Regional exposure (Southeast Asia, US, Australia, or Greater China) and networks are viewed favorably.
  • Candidates currently based in Southeast Asia are strongly preferred, but we are open to Sydney, San Francisco or other key markets.
  • This is a partner-track opportunity, and no finance/investment experience is necessary.

title: Director of Platform Engineering
description:
Role purpose

The Director of Platform Engineering is the single accountable owner for the platform and data engineering capabilities used across every product domain in the business. The role consolidates Platform Engineering and Data Platform under one senior leader, and runs those capabilities as internal products with named service expectations, a published roadmap, and a regular review cadence with Domain Directors. This is a new role, created to separate architectural authority from operational delivery. The Chief Architect sets technical direction; this role owns the delivery, reliability, and adoption of the shared capabilities that direction depends on. The two roles are peers.

Reporting and scope

• Direct reports: Platform Engineering Manager, Data Platform Lead. Indirect organisation of approximately 15 engineers at steady state.

• Internal customers: Three product domains (360, Assure and Learn) plus internal engineering and operations teams.

• Peer relationships: Chief Architect, Domain Directors, Product Directors, Head of Business Technology

Key responsibilities

Run shared capabilities as products. Define service expectations, roadmaps, and adoption metrics for Platform Engineering and Data Platform. Be the single named owner for operational performance: incident response, SLOs, capacity, cost-to-serve, and roadmap delivery.

Earn the trust of Domain Directors. Treat domain teams as customers. Establish a regular review cadence with each Domain Director. Where a shared capability is not fit for a domain's needs, lead the work to fix it rather than defending the status quo.

Partner with the Chief Architect. Translate architectural direction (multi-tenancy, AI paved roads, Technology Radar) into deliverable platform capabilities on a documented timeline. Surface implementation realities that should inform the architectural roadmap.

Manage cloud cost. Own the FinOps practice for the platform estate. Drive unit cost down without compromising reliability and give domain teams the visibility they need to manage their own consumption.

Build the team. Coach, develop, and where needed recruit the sub-function leads. Build a team that can operate the function without the Director being the bottleneck for every decision.

What success looks like at twelve months

• Platform Engineering and Data Platform operate under published service expectations, with a regular review cadence with each Domain Director.

• Incident response, SLO attainment, and cloud unit cost are tracked, reported, and trending in the right direction.

• Platform compliance evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and IRAP is generated as a by-product of normal operations rather than as a separate audit project.

• The two sub-function leads are operating as a coherent leadership team with clear ownership of their domains.

Essential experience

• Five or more years of engineering leadership, with at least three years owning a platform, infrastructure, or shared services function at director level or above.

• Demonstrated experience running engineering capabilities as internal products, including setting service expectations, managing roadmaps, and being accountable for adoption.

• Track record in a multi-product SaaS environment, with credible experience of the trade-offs between centralised platform investment and domain team autonomy.

• Direct accountability for AWS cloud infrastructure at scale, including FinOps practices and unit cost management.

• Experience as the engineering owner for at least one of SOC 2, ISO 27001, or an equivalent regulated compliance regime.

• Track record of building and developing engineering teams, including hiring at managerial level.

Desirable experience

• Exposure to data platform engineering, including the operational realities of running analytics and data pipelines as a shared capability.

• Experience in EHS, GRC, or another regulated B2B SaaS domain.

• Experience leading a transition from federated to centralised shared services, including the change management involved.

How you work

• Comfortable with productive friction. Architecture and delivery are inherently in tension. You see that tension as where the work gets done, not as a problem to be eliminated.

• Customer mindset toward internal teams. You earn adoption by being genuinely useful, not by mandate. You would rather change a shared capability than win an argument about it.

• Operationally credible. You can be in the detail of an incident or a roadmap commitment when the situation requires it, without making yourself the bottleneck for normal operations.

• Direct. You give and receive feedback clearly, and you are willing to disagree with peers in the room rather than after the meeting.


Why join Evotix?

  • Competitive Compensation: Enjoy a competitive base salary and company-based performance bonus.
  • Time to Recharge: Unlimited Annual Leave because we trust you to balance your work and wellbeing. (AMER/EMEA)
  • Financial Future: Generous tiered 401k plan that increases over time. (AMER)
  • Support for You: Access to our Employee Assistance Program, including mental health, legal, and financial guidance.
  • Growth Opportunities: Educational benefits to help you keep learning and growing.
  • Team Culture: Regular team events, an inclusive environment, and a shared commitment to making an impact.


Ready to Make a Difference?
If you’re a bold, results-driven leader who thrives on challenges, loves scaling success, and is passionate about making a difference—we want to hear from you!

Thank you for your interest. Please note, we are not seeking support from external recruitment agencies at this time. Direct applications from candidates are warmly welcomed.

title: Associate Director, CMC Analytical Development
description:
Overview

  • Lead analytical development for small-molecule API and based drug products from IND-enabling studies through NDA readiness in a virtual, outsourced model.
  • Direct analytical methods, stability, specifications, impurity controls, and performance testing for drug substance and drug product.
  • Manage CDMOs, CROs, budgets, and submissions against clinical and regulatory timelines.

Responsibilities

  • Analytical Development
  • Drive overall control strategy and Justification of specification for release and stability
  • Develop phase-appropriate analytical and control strategies for drug substance, excipients, intermediates, and drug products focused on oral dosage forms.
  • Oversee method development, transfer, validation, and lifecycle management for assay, impurities, chiral purity, water, and physical characterization.
  • Lead residual-solvent risk assessment and controls, including headspace GC, and elemental-impurity risk assessments and testing, including ICP-MS, in line with ICH requirements.
  • Direct ICH stability, forced-degradation, reference-standard, specification, comparability, and shelf-life activities.
  • Set extractables and leachables strategies for container-closure and product-contact materials; oversee external GC-MS, LC-MS, and ICP-MS studies.
  • Define analytical testing requirement for container closure involved
  • Define microbiological and antimicrobial related requirements
  • Guide cleaning verification related method development
  • Support analytical methods required in any other formulation and process development
  • Involve in management of reference standards and API inventory required at CDMO
  • Dissolution and Biopharmaceutics
  • Develop discriminating and, when appropriate, biorelevant dissolution methods for oral dosage forms across BCS Classes I-IV.
  • Assess apparatus, media, pH, surfactant, sink conditions, precipitation risk, particle size, solid form, formulation variables, and manufacturing-process parameters.
  • Support clinically relevant specifications, dissolution-profile comparisons, formulation and site bridging, in vitro-in vivo relationships, and BCS-based biowaiver strategies.
  • External Partner and Quality Oversight
  • Select and govern CDMOs, CROs, and testing laboratories; define scopes, review proposals, manage timelines and budgets, and monitor technical performance.
  • Review protocols, methods, specifications, reports, certificates of analysis, validation packages, stability data, and batch documentation.
  • Lead OOS, OOT, deviation, change-control, CAPA, and data-integrity investigations; support vendor audits and inspection readiness.
  • Regulatory and Compendial Compliance
  • Apply cGMP, applicable ICH guidance, and dosage-form requirements in USP-NF, Ph. Eur., JP, and other relevant pharmacopoeias to methods, specifications, and control strategies.
  • Author and review analytical CMC content for INDs, IMPDs, NDAs, amendments, annual reports, briefing documents, and health-authority responses.
  • Prepare CTD Module 3 analytical sections covering specifications, procedures, validation, batch analyses, impurities, reference standards, dissolution, container-closure systems, and stability.
  • Cross Functional Leadership
  • Represent Analytical Development on CMC program teams and communicate risks, recommendations, timelines, and resource needs to internal leaders and external partners.
  • Collaborate with formulation, process chemistry, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, toxicology, packaging, clinical supply, project management, and finance.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent with a minimum of 12 years of relevant experience, or Pharm.D., master's degree, or Ph.D. with at least 8 years of relevant experience.
  • Analytical development experience with small-molecule drug substances and oral drug products from early development through late-stage or NDA readiness.
  • Experience with HPLC/UPLC, GC/headspace GC, LC-MS, GC-MS, ICP-MS, dissolution, stability-indicating methods, residual solvents, elemental impurities, and extractables and leachables.
  • Experience developing discriminating dissolution methods and applying BCS principles to compounds with varied solubility and permeability.
  • Strong knowledge of cGMP, ICH guidance, and compendial requirements for oral dosage forms, including USP-NF, Ph. Eur., and JP.
  • Direct experience authoring and reviewing analytical CTD Module 3 content for INDs, IMPDs, and NDAs.
  • Demonstrated oversight of outsourced laboratories and CDMOs, including method transfer, investigations, timelines, budgets, and vendor performance.
  • Manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing program needs.
  • Communicate clearly in writing and in cross-functional meetings.
  • Exercise sound scientific judgment and close attention to detail.
  • Work effectively under schedule pressure in a virtual environment.
  • Periodic travel to CDMOs, contract laboratories, manufacturing sites, and company meetings may be required.

Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated salary range for this position is $150,000 to $190,000. Actual compensation may vary based on factors including experience, qualifications, skills, and business needs.

In addition to base salary, SK Life Science offers a competitive benefits package, including a 401(k) plan with company match and medical, dental, and vision coverage. Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and may be modified at the Company's discretion.

title: Senior Data Engineer - Toronto
description:
Senior Data Engineer

Toronto

Position Overview:

As a Senior Data Engineer on our Data & Analytics Team, you will be a hands‑on technical leader responsible for designing, building, operating, and continuously improving scalable, secure, and reliable data solutions. The role will help modernize Trisura’ s data platform, enable trusted analytics and reporting, and establish engineering standards across ingestion, transformation, orchestration, deployment, monitoring, data quality, and documentation.

Working closely with Data & Analytics, application teams, architects, analysts, governance, and business stakeholders, the Senior Data Engineer will translate business requirements into reusable data products and production‑grade solutions across Microsoft Fabric, Azure, SQL Server, Power BI, and related technologies.

What you will do:

  • Design, build, test, deploy, and support scalable batch and near‑real‑time data pipelines for structured, semi‑structured, and unstructured data using Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Factory, SSIS, SQL Server, Azure SQL, cloud storage, and other enterprise data sources.
  • Develop modern data engineering solutions using Microsoft Fabric capabilities such as Lakehouse, Warehouse, OneLake, Copy Jobs, Notebooks, Dataflow Gen2, and related services, applying layered bronze/silver/gold architecture patterns where appropriate.
  • Develop robust, reusable ETL/ELT and data transformation solutions using T‑SQL, Python, PySpark, and Spark SQL, including incremental loading, Change Data Capture (CDC), schema evolution, reconciliation, restart/recovery, idempotency, and error‑handling patterns.
  • Design dimensional, relational, and Lakehouse data models that support analytics, operational and regulatory reporting, self‑service analytics, and downstream system integrations.
  • Ensure production reliability by implementing monitoring, alerting, logging, data quality controls, reconciliation, metadata, lineage, auditability, and operational support procedures.
  • Optimize SQL, Spark, pipeline, and storage workloads for performance, scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency while applying security and privacy best practices, including least‑privilege access, managed identities, service principals, secrets management, secure connectivity, and environment separation.
  • Implement source control, automated deployment, and CI/CD practices using Git, Azure DevOps, and Microsoft Fabric deployment capabilities, and participate in code reviews, testing, release planning, incident resolution, root‑cause analysis, and post‑implementation reviews.
  • Develop reusable engineering standards, frameworks, templates, patterns, and technical documentation to improve consistency, maintainability, and operational support across the data platform.
  • Partner with Power BI developers, analysts, business stakeholders, Data Governance, and other technology teams to translate business requirements into trusted, well‑structured data solutions and clearly communicate dependencies, risks, and technical trade‑offs.
  • Support the modernization and migration of legacy SSIS, SSRS, Azure Data Factory, SQL‑based, and other data integration workloads to strategic cloud and Microsoft Fabric platforms.

What You Bring:

Core Skills:

  • Strong ownership, accountability, and a focus on delivering reliable, maintainable data solutions.
  • Ability to lead technical design discussions, mentor other engineers, and promote engineering best practices.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts to technical and non‑technical audiences.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast‑paced environment, manage competing priorities, and independently drive work from requirements through production support.
  • A collaborative and customer‑focused mindset when working with business stakeholders, analysts, developers, architects, vendors, and operational teams.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with a focus on root‑cause analysis, automation, and continuous improvement.

Technical Expertise:

  • Advanced SQL and T‑SQL skills, including complex querying, stored procedures, views, indexing, execution‑plan analysis, performance tuning, and query optimization.
  • Strong Python skills for data engineering, automation, testing, API integration, and file processing, with hands‑on experience in PySpark and Spark SQL preferred.
  • Hands‑on experience with Microsoft Fabric and Azure data services, including Lakehouse, Warehouse, OneLake, Delta tables, pipelines, notebooks, Azure Data Factory, Azure SQL Database/Managed Instance, Azure Data Lake Storage, and Key Vault.
  • Strong understanding of modern data architecture and engineering patterns, including data warehousing, Lakehouse architecture, dimensional modeling, medallion architecture, ETL/ELT, incremental processing, and enterprise data integration.
  • Experience with Git‑based source control, branching and pull‑request practices, automated testing, CI/CD, and environment‑specific configuration and deployment.
  • Experience designing secure data solutions using Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, service principals, role‑based access control, secrets management, and least‑privilege principles.
  • Knowledge of data observability and governance practices, including logging, monitoring, alerting, pipeline metrics, reconciliation, metadata, lineage, data quality, retention, reference/master data, and audit requirements.
  • Working knowledge of Power BI and semantic model consumption patterns; experience with DAX is considered an asset.
  • Experience integrating enterprise databases, REST APIs, JSON, CSV, Parquet, Delta, SFTP, and other file‑based or application data sources.
  • Experience with PostgreSQL and legacy Microsoft technologies such as SSIS and SSRS is an asset, particularly in modernization and migration initiatives.
  • Ability to develop clean, modular, testable, maintainable, and well‑documented production‑quality code.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree, college diploma, or equivalent practical experience in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in data engineering, data integration, data warehousing, analytics engineering, or related roles, including ownership of production data solutions.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and delivering end‑to‑end data solutions rather than only developing individual ETL components or reports.
  • Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex production data issues and improving platform reliability, performance, and maintainability.
  • Experience providing technical leadership, mentoring, code review, solution design, or engineering standards is strongly preferred.
  • Experience in Insurance or another regulated financial‑services environment is strongly preferred.
  • Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Engineer, Azure, Power BI, or related Microsoft certifications are considered an asset.

Location

  • Downtown Toronto – Hybrid

Salary

  • The maximum potential base salary for this position is $125,000

This salary range reflects the expected base compensation for the role across Canada. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and scope of responsibilities. Trisura provides this range in good faith in accordance with applicable legislation.
