title: Principal Architect - Payments & Ledger
description:
YouTrip is the leading and fastest-growing multi-currency payment platform in Asia Pacific. In 2018, we pioneered the region's first multi-currency digital wallet. Now, YouTrip is the #1 multi-currency digital wallet trusted by millions across the region, processing over US$15 billion in total payment value annually.

Our consumer and business propositions – YouTrip and YouBiz – empower individuals and businesses with inclusive, accessible, and affordable financial solutions. YouTrip has raised over US$110 million to date, including its recent Series B round led by global venture capital firm Lightspeed Venture Partners—underscoring strong investor confidence in its mission to transform digital financial services across the Asia Pacific.

Recognised as World Economic Forum’s Global Innovator 2025, CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies (2025, 2024), and LinkedIn’s Top Startup (2024, 2023), YouTrip is dedicated to creating the next generation of digital finance services for consumers and businesses.

Valuing an entrepreneurial culture of diversity and inclusion, we are seeking driven individuals to join our fast-growing regional team as we push the boundaries of innovative fintech solutions.

Job Description: Principal Architect, Payments & Ledger

You'll own the architectural direction for money movement end to end: multi-currency wallets and balances, the core ledger, card issuing and authorisation, in-app FX, overseas transfers and payouts, treasury and pre-funding, settlement and reconciliation, and the shared platform services underneath them. Your remit covers both YouTrip (consumer) and YouBiz (business), across every market we operate in.

Responsibilities:

  • The Ledger - Double-entry design, chart of accounts, sub-ledger boundaries, immutability and correction rules, multi-currency representation, precision and rounding policy, and how balances are derived or stored. You'll define how we handle authorisation holds, reversals, partial and incremental captures, refunds, FX revaluation and unreconciled positions, and you'll be able to explain and defend those choices to Finance, auditors and regulators.
  • Money movement correctness - Idempotency, exactly-once outcomes on top of at-least-once messaging, clear state machines for every transaction type, and well-defined failure, retry, timeout and compensation paths. For every integration, the question "what happens if the partner succeeds and we fail?" should have a written answer that you own.
  • Card issuing - Architecture for authorisation, clearing and settlement as a Mastercard Principal Member, including real-time authorisation on the scheme's critical path, stand-in processing, authorisation expiry, disputes and chargebacks, tokenisation for Apple Pay and Google Pay, virtual and physical card lifecycle, and the strict latency and availability targets that come with it.
  • FX and multi-currency wallets - Rate sourcing, quoting and rate locking, spread and exposure management, in-app currency exchange across our wallet currencies, and pre-funding and liquidity models that keep customers' balances safe and available.
  • Cross-border transfers - Corridor architecture, payout rail integrations (local real-time rails, bank transfers, SWIFT and partner networks), pre-funding and nostro design, and sanctions and AML screening built in as a core design constraint, not an afterthought.
  • Reconciliation and settlement - We treat reconciliation as an architecture problem, not an operations task. You'll design systems where breaks are rare, spotted within minutes, and traceable to a clear cause, across multiple time zones, currencies and partners.
  • Non-functional requirements - Latency, throughput, availability and cost as design targets with numbers attached. Clear, written decisions on where eventual consistency is acceptable and where it isn't. Recovery, replay and backfill as built-in capabilities.
  • Standards and technical judgement - Engineering and coding standards, architecture reviews for significant changes, and architecture documentation that engineers actually build from. You'll write decision records that capture the reasoning and the options rejected, and keep them current.
  • Partners and vendors - Technical evaluation and ongoing oversight of card processors, scheme connectivity, banking and settlement partners, FX liquidity providers, payout partners, KYC and screening vendors, and core infrastructure. You'll know their systems' failure modes as well as their own architects do.
  • Growing technical leaders - You'll mentor tech leads and senior engineers from day one and lead mostly through influence. As the function matures, you'll build and lead a small architecture group.

Requirements

  • Deep payments and ledger experience (essential) - You've designed or substantially rebuilt a production financial ledger. You can speak from real experience about journal design, posting models, balance consistency and correction strategies, including what happens when they go wrong.
  • Card issuing expertise - Hands-on experience with card scheme integrations (ideally Mastercard), issuer processing, authorisation flows, clearing files, and disputes.
  • A builder, not just an advisor - You've written production code at scale, and your work sits behind systems that handled real traffic and real money. Your authority comes from having shipped.
  • Range from system to field level - You're equally comfortable designing distributed settlement flows and deciding the type and precision of a single amount field, often in the same week.
  • Regulated-environment fluency - Experience with safeguarding and customer fund segregation, payment and e-money licensing, data residency, auditability and technology risk requirements, ideally including MAS and other Asia Pacific regulators. You design ahead of regulatory and scheme changes instead of reacting to them.
  • Multi-market experience - You've built systems that operate across several countries, currencies and regulators at once.
  • Strong writing - Clear, structured, opinionated documents that remain useful long after the meeting ends. Documentation is part of the work, not a follow-up task.
  • Opinions you can defend - Clear positions on design patterns, standards and trade-offs, explained just as well to a new graduate as to the board.
  • Credibility with partners - You can tell when a vendor's recommendation serves them more than us, and you can make that case with evidence.
  • Experience with Golang, event-driven architectures and cloud-native infrastructure is a plus.

What This Role Is Not

This isn't a diagramming role, and it isn't a review gate that approves other people's work without contributing to it. It's also not an engineering management role with large headcount or delivery ownership, though its influence is comparable. If you're looking to run a large organisation, we have other roles for that.


What You Can Expect From Us

  • The chance to shape the core money platform of Asia Pacific's leading multi-currency wallet, used by millions of people and businesses.
  • Some of the most interesting payments challenges in the region, across multiple markets, currencies, partners and regulators.
  • A company that is committed to getting the architecture right, not just shipping fast.
  • A culture that values technical craft, direct feedback and getting things done.


To Apply

If you're interested in this role, click Apply Now and send us your CV. Due to the high volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: CDOT Employees Only: Crested Butte TM II ($500/mo housing)
description:
Department Information

CDOT Employees Only: Transportation Maintenance II - Crested Butte


This position is only open to current, classified, permanent CDOT employees.


The eligible list created from this announcement may be used to fill current and future vacancies which may become available during the life of this list. Please note that the first step in the comparative analysis process for this position will be the TM II job knowledge written assessment. You must have taken the test within the last year and received a score of at least 60% to pass the written assessment and be placed on the eligible list. NOTE: If you took and passed the test more than a year ago, you will need to retake the test and receive a score of at least 60%.


This vacancy is a lead worker TM II that will be located out of Crested Butte, CO.

Total annual compensation for this position is $59,940 ($53,940 base pay and $6,000 housing stipend).


Base pay for this position is $2,074.62/biweekly ($53,940 - 54,000/annually). There are 26 biweekly pay periods in a year. This location is also eligible for an additional $500/month housing stipend. The annualized hourly rate for this position is $25.93/hour, with an overtime rate of $38.90/hour.

CDOT for All

CDOT’s strength is our people, and our commitment to our people is to shape, support, and sustain the employee experience, and ultimately, create a supportive workplace where everyone, regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, education, disability, socio-economic status, or any other identity, has the opportunity to thrive.


The eligible list created from this announcement may be used to fill current and future vacancies for a period of up to 6 months.

Description of Job

This position is responsible for leading a patrol and overseeing general maintenance activities for a designated area. The TM II also performs skilled, specialized heavy construction equipment operation and heavy manual labor under hazardous and adverse conditions. This position is responsible for maintaining facilities to as near original conditions as it was constructed as well as ensuring that all equipment is safe and operable.


Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Perform the daily planning and scheduling of activities in assigned worked area; develop work plans for employees on the patrol; review work progress, identify training needs, and provide feedback, on-the-job training and mentoring; provide performance appraisal input / recommendations; conduct tailgate safety talks for employees;

  • Ensure patrol attends all required personnel training, safety classes, and informational training; perform worksite, night, and roadway inventory inspections;

  • Lead, perform and assist in maintaining roadway surface by hand patching, roto-milling, machine patching, crack-sealing, blading existing unpaved shoulders, building or restoring unpaved shoulders, stock piling, etc.;

  • Lead, perform and assist in the maintenance of road side facilities by drainage structure cleaning, repair and replacement, maintenance of streambeds and ditches, slope repair, dirt drifts, mud and rock slide cleanup, fence, gate and sound barrier maintenance, litter-barrel and trash clean up, rock run, machine sweeping, and hand sweeping;

  • Lead, perform and assist in traffic services, such as the maintenance, replacement, and installation of single post sign, delineator and reference post, metal guard rail, concrete rail, pavement marking or removal, roadway warning devices, energy attenuator, and courtesy assistance;

  • Lead, perform and assist in the maintenance of roadside appearance by vegetation control, hand mowing, weeding, tree trimming and tree removal;

  • Lead, perform and assist in bridge / structure maintenance and repair by visual inspection, cleaning/washing, deck repair, crack and joint sealing- rigid bridge deck, roto-milling flexible bridge decks, roto-milling rigid bridge decks, crack sealing flexible decks, bridge superstructure maintenance and repair, painting, bridge/structure bearing maintenance repair, bridge substructure maintenance repair, approach slabs and slope protection, and deck expansion device maintenance and repair;

  • Lead, perform and assist in snow and ice control by snow removal, traction application, ice control, stock piling, and snow fence installation and repair;

  • Lead, perform and assist in the maintenance and repair of equipment, buildings, and grounds upkeep;

  • Complete required paperwork and reports; use SAP to enter work orders, timesheet entries, and other items on a regular basis.

  • Trim and remove trees; remove graffiti;

  • Use a variety of light to heavy equipment;

  • Ensure patrol uses proper equipment and PPE;

  • Assist other patrols as needed;

  • Other duties as assigned.


Work Environment:

  • Exposure to loud noise

  • Exposure to fumes, odors, gasses, dusts, etc. that may affect breathing, eyes and skin

  • Required to use appropriate personal protective equipment

  • Required to work with chemicals and cleaning products

  • Some equipment requires the use of respirators

  • Work in close proximity to heavy traffic

  • Use of ladders and scissor lifts for heights of approximately 10 – 20’

  • Required to use various hand tools and to operate heavy equipment, such as backhoe, tractor, bucket truck, forklift, skid steer, loader, aerial devices and other equipment

  • Required to drive CDOT vehicles

  • Exposure to High Voltage (anything over 600 V) and electrical shock

  • Some of the positions are NIGHTS ONLY and others are WEEKEND positions

  • Frequently respond to emergencies outside of regular work hours and may work overtime including weekends and holidays

  • Must be willing and be physically able to work in extreme temperatures (hot and cold), variable weather conditions, and at varying elevations up to 12,000 feet for long periods of time

  • Required to use computers to accomplish everyday work duties

  • The average work week is 40 hours a week, with periodic overtime due to emergencies or inclement weather

  • Must be able to read, understand, and follow oral and written instructions.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

Minimum Qualifications

  • At least three (3) years of experience in road/highway maintenance

Examples of road/highway maintenance experience: repairing potholes; performing asphalt or concrete paving operations; operating heavy equipment such as bulldozers, motor graders, backhoes, front end loaders and other heavy equipment to repair and/or maintain roads; maintaining right-of-way fences; performing street striping and marking; performing mechanical mowing along the roadside (e.g. handheld weed eater up to a 15' rotary mower); performing bridge; roadside ditch and culvert cleaning and maintenance; installing and/or maintaining roadway signs or guardrail; operating mechanical sweepers; conducting traffic control; or performing mechanical snow removal (gator up to a tandem truck).


Please note: The required experience must be substantiated within the work experience section of your application. “See Resume” statements on the application or resumes in lieu of a complete application may not be accepted. Additional information submitted after the closing date of this announcement will not be considered in the review of your application. In addition, part-time work will be prorated.


Conditions of Employment: The following conditions must be met and maintained in order to be employed and to continue employment at CDOT in this position, unless exempted by the Maintenance Superintendent or Traffic Program Engineer.

  • Must pass a pre-employment screening which may include social security number trace, criminal records check, public court records check, educational records, and driving records checks. More information in the supplemental information section.

  • Must possess and maintain a valid Commercial Driver's License Class A or B with no restriction on air brakes that allows operation within Colorado.

  • You may be required to obtain a Hazardous Materials endorsement within 6 months to 1 year as a condition of appointment.

  • May be required to pass a controlled substance test (i.e. drug test), and DOT physical through our medical provider.

  • May be required to work overtime including weekends and holidays.

  • Essential Services Designation – Required to report without delay or interruption to provide essential or emergency services outside regular work hours to ensure health, safety, and welfare.

  • May be required to live within thirty (30) minutes' driving time in normal weather conditions to be able to respond in a timely manner after notified to report to work. Knowledge of an emergency or hazardous condition may be considered to be notification to report to work station.

  • Must provide the supervisor with a telephone number where you can be reached for the purposes of responding to an emergency.

  • Required to attend training one week out of each year online or in Aurora.



Preferred Qualifications

The Exceptional Applicant will be dedicated to a career in the transportation field and possess proven ability or accomplishment in the following:

  • Demonstrated success with the duties as listed in the Description of the Job section;

  • Years of State service experience related to the duties of this position;

  • Demonstrated experience in scheduling and planning daily work activities for subordinates;

  • Comprehensive knowledge of the Emergency Response Guidelines, Manual of Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) and supplement to set traffic control for road projects through different terrain, Colorado’s Chain Law, Federal Motor Carriers Safety Regulation, Colorado Commercial Driver’s License Manual, MLOS standards, M & S Standards, and CDOT Policies and Procedures;

  • Possess and maintain in good standing a Colorado CDL Class A or B with endorsements such as hazardous materials and tanker;

  • Extensive experience safely and effectively operating and training others on several types of heavy equipment, such as front end loaders, tandem trucks, backhoes;

  • Extensive experience effectively using several types of hand tools;

  • Extensive experience performing physically demanding work assignments;

  • Strong positive and can-do attitude;

  • Strong commitment to safety;

  • Strong oral and written communication;

  • Ability to effectively communicate with CDOT staff and others, sometimes in safety situations where quick communication is essential;

  • Self-starter and motivated to accomplish assigned tasks;

  • Ability to react safely and properly in emergency situations;

  • Ability to quickly learn with minimal direction;

  • Ability to adapt to changes in work assignments and environments;

  • Ability to effectively perform as a leader and mentor to employees;

  • Strong customer service skills;

  • Strong project management and work scheduling skills;

  • Effective interpersonal and relationship building skills;

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy;

  • Strong analytical, reasoning, troubleshooting, and problem solving skills;

  • Ability to work effectively in both independent and team situations;

  • Familiarity with SAP, MS Office Suite, Gmail, the knowledge and know how to use computers, and the ability to quickly learn new software.

Supplemental Information

Applicant Checklist: Complete Applications must include the following documents:

  1. A complete CDOT Application for Announced Vacancy (please submit online using the green 'APPLY' button at the top of this announcement)

  2. A complete Supplemental Questionnaire (The questionnaire is part of the online application. You will be prompted to answer them as you are completing your online application.)


Please note that you may redact information on your attachments that identifies your age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.


Only complete applications submitted by the closing date for this announcement will be given consideration. Every effort must be made to submit all application materials by the announcement close date. Where unusual circumstances prevent timely acquisition of transcripts, they must be submitted within five business days of the announcement close date. Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of a completed application. Failure to submit properly completed documents by the closing date of this announcement may result in your application being rejected.


The State of Colorado strives to create a Colorado for All by building and maintaining workplaces that value and respect all Coloradans through a commitment to equal opportunity and hiring based on merit and fitness.

The State is resolute in non-discriminatory practices in everything we do, including hiring, employment, and advancement opportunities.


Notifications:

All correspondence regarding your status in the selection/examination process will be via email. Include your current working email address on your application and check your email frequently as you could receive time sensitive correspondence regarding this position. We highly recommend that you set up your email to accept messages from "" and "info@governmentjobs.com" addresses. It is your responsibility to ensure that your email will accept these notices and/or review your junk mail and spam filtered email. Immediately after you submit your application you should receive an email that confirms that you successfully submitted an application for this position.   2. Colorado Revised Statutes require that state employees are hired and promoted based on merit and fitness through a comparative analysis process.

  • The comparative analysis process for this position will be the TM II job knowledge written assessment. You must receive a score of at least 60% to pass the written assessment and be placed on the eligible list.

  1. A top group, up to six candidates, will be invited to schedule an interview with the hiring manager.



Transfer, Non-Disciplinary Demotion or Reinstatement

If you believe that you are eligible to be considered as a transfer, non-disciplinary demotion, or reinstatement to this vacancy, you must submit a completed application following the directions in this job announcement and you will be included in the selection process along with other qualified applicants. If you are the finalist for this position after the selection process, Human Resources will confirm your eligibility to be appointed as a transfer, non-disciplinary demotion, or reinstatement applicant.

These reports may be obtained at any time after receipt of the applicant's authorization. Appeal Rights

title: 🩺 Non-VR General Practitioner | $150/hr | QLD, NSW, VIC, SA, WA
description:
If you're non-VR, where you work and which program you're on decide whether you can bill Medicare at all. These clinics are in Distribution Priority Areas, and we'll confirm the DPA status of your exact site before any offer is made.

The work is chronic and complex care across Medicare and DVA billing streams, with a Chronic Care Team behind every patient: physio, exercise physiology, dietetics, podiatry, OT and care coordination. Admin and care coordinators carry the paperwork, so your time goes on patients.

The money

  • $150/hr, at the upper end of the non-VR market

Locations

  • QLD: Ipswich, Enoggera, Caboolture
  • NSW: Newcastle, Penrith, Fairfield
  • VIC: Frankston, Werribee, Laverton
  • SA: Gawler, Murray Bridge
  • WA: Rockingham, Joondalup

Requirements

Your Medicare pathway

  • 19AB, if you trained overseas or studied here as a temporary resident: you'll need a DPA exemption. You apply for it with your Medicare provider number, and it's tied to the practice location. Services Australia assesses it within 28 working days, and you bill Medicare when both are in place.
  • 19AA, if you're an Australian citizen or permanent resident: you must be enrolled in an approved 3GA program before you start. At our sites that's usually the Pre-Fellowship Program. It costs nothing and is open year round, and every states Rural Workforce Agency processes it in around 28 business days.
  • Trained overseas and now a PR or citizen? Both 19AA and 19AB apply to you.
  • DVA billing opens once your provider number is active.

On Fellowship. PFP gets you billing Medicare and building general practice experience. It isn't a Fellowship pathway on its own, so you'll join a college-led program such as AGPT when you're ready to sit your exams.

You'll need

  • General AHPRA registration
  • PGY3 or above
  • Right to work in Australia
  • For PFP: no previous enrolment in a 3GA program

Benefits

  • DVA and Coordinated Veterans' Care experience is not essentialas onboarding is provided
  • Independent contractor, rates exclusive of GST.

Not sure which pathway applies to you? Call or text Stuart Smith, Head of Talent, on 0481 179 106, or email stuart.s@pro-active.com.au. We'll work it out on the call.

title: We are looking for a Social Impact intern to join our studio in Copenhagen in January/Febuary 2027
description:
We are looking for a Social Impact intern to join our studio in Copenhagen in January/February 2027
Copenhagen, Denmark

Why do we need you?

We are looking for a Social Impact intern to join our team!

As our new intern you will be part of our multidisciplinary R&D department, working alongside architects, engineers, social scientists, computational designers, sustainability experts and PhDs to advance sustainability within the built environment. You will work directly with our Head of Social Impact, contributing to international projects of varying scales and typologies, focusing on the experiential qualities of the built environment and the impact of design on individuals and communities.

You will work with qualitative and quantitative data, conduct user and stakeholder analysis, translate findings into written and graphic material, and develop tailored strategies for inclusion to support our projects.

What are we looking for?
We value open-minded and curious people who are passionate about advancing inclusion in our cities and designed spaces. We expect you to be able to think critically and holistically about design, engaging constructively in conversations that address cultural nuance, bias, diversity, accessibility, sustainability, demographic change, generational shifts, social cohesion and more.

An ideal candidate has a background or experience that can bridge between social sciences, humanities and design, motivation to learn, great communication skills (writing, graphics, oral) and the ability to thrive in a dynamic work environment, at times moving between several projects simultaneously.

At minimum, you need to have completed your bachelor's degree, possess strong communication skills, proficiency in Adobe InDesign and Illustrator, competence in diagramming and graphic presentations. Experience with qualitative research methods and socio-spatial analysis are a big advantage.

Commitment required is 6 months, with possibility to extend. This internship is intended to be a part of your studies and requires you to be enrolled as a student.

About the internship
Joining our Copenhagen office, you will be part of a company working with international projects of all scales and sizes. We offer intern positions for 6-12 months, with the opportunity for extension. You must be enrolled as a student for the full duration. Start date: January 2027. The internship is paid.

How do you apply?
Submit your CV, cover letter and/or portfolio (max 10 MB) before 30.10.2026. Interviews are conducted on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply early.

Please note that we reserve the right to take down the applications early depending on the volume of applications that we receive.

About Henning Larsen
Henning Larsen is an international design studio with strong Nordic roots and values at the core of who we are. With over 650 employees, the design community spans studios in eight countries including Denmark, the United States, Singapore, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Australia and Hong Kong.

We believe that creativity in design thinking is propelled through an active use of data and knowledge in the process. United by a mission to craft sustainable societies where people and nature flourish, our partnership with the Ramboll Group builds on deep interdisciplinary expertise. Together, Henning Larsen and Ramboll have access to the world's leading designers, experts, technology, and digitalization, enabling us to deliver world-class knowledge in a local context to create impactful design benefitting our clients and society at large.

title: Graphic Designer
description:
We are looking for an exceptionally talented Graphic Designer to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for developing high-quality creative and visual communications that support Side's global brand, marketing and commercial objectives.

This role will work across brand, presentations, digital, events, motion and corporate communications. You will collaborate closely with the wider marketing team to translate creative briefs, business ideas and complex ideas into compelling and effective visual communications.

You will play a key role in supporting the continued development of Side's client-facing and corporate presentation materials. There will be the opportunity to partner across disciplines and business functions to transform content into engaging visual stories.

    • Work closely with Marketing, Sales, Sales Enablement, Commercial Leadership, Finance, HR, Communications and teams across Side's global studios and service lines.
    • Collaborate with other creative resources, agencies, web developers, event suppliers and production partners where required.
    • Develop high-quality creative and visual assets across Side's marketing and comms.
    • Apply and evolve Side's visual identity consistently across digital, print and physical assets.
    • Support campaigns, service launches, thought leadership and other marketing initiatives from concept through to final delivery.
    • Create high-quality client, sales and executive presentations, moving beyond template formatting to deliver strong visual storytelling.
    • Provide design support for corporate, commercial and financial reporting, including data visualization and recurring reporting templates.
    • Evolve reusable PowerPoint templates, presentation systems and visual assets that enable teams to create consistently high-quality materials.
    • Design creative for websites and digital campaigns using Figma and Adobe Creative Suite.
    • Create motion graphics, animated content and short-form video for campaigns, social media, presentations and events.
    • Work effectively with web developers and external partners to translate creative concepts into digital experiences.
    • Develop creative concepts and production-ready artwork for exhibitions and client events.
    • Design booth graphics, signage, graphics, digital screens and supporting event collateral.
    • Explore and integrate generative AI and emerging creative technologies into professional design workflows, aligning with company policy and brand guidelines.
    • Manage multiple briefs and deadlines within established Marketing workflows.

Requirements

The ideal candidate will combine strong graphic design fundamentals with excellent presentation

and information design skills and capabilities across digital design, motion/video, large-format

design and emerging creative technologies.

    • Approximately 3–5 years' professional graphic design experience within an in-house team, agency or similar creative environment.
    • Strong portfolio demonstrating excellent graphic design, conceptual thinking and visual storytelling across a range of formats.
    • Advanced Adobe Creative Suite skills, particularly Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.
    • Strong PowerPoint and presentation design skills, with the ability to transform business content into compelling client-facing visual communications.
    • Strong Figma and digital design capability, with an understanding of responsive and web design principles.
    • Experience creating motion graphics and editing video using After Effects, Premiere Pro or equivalent tools.
    • Experience designing large-format, exhibition or environmental graphics and preparing artwork for production.
    • Strong understanding of typography, layout, visual hierarchy, information design and data visualization.
    • Familiarity with generative AI and emerging creative technologies and an interest in applying these to professional creative workflows.
    • Excellent communication, organization and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
    • Experience within games, technology, B2B marketing or corporate/financial reporting would be advantageous.
    • Degree, diploma or equivalent qualification in Graphic Design, Visual Communication or a related discipline or equivalent professional experience.
    • A strong portfolio demonstrating high-quality graphic design, conceptual thinking and visual storytelling across digital and print formats.

Benefits

What we offer:

  • The opportunity to join our growing business at an exciting time.
  • Dynamic and entrepreneurial culture.

Who we are:

Side is a global video game development and services provider, offering technical and creative solutions to many of the largest developers and studios around the world. Founded in 2009 and drawing on 30+ years' experience from our parent company in Japan, Side has since grown to become a global force with 15+ studios in over a dozen countries across North America, Europe, South America, and Asia.

Our industry-leading services include game development, art production, audio production, quality assurance, localization, localization QA, player support, community management, and datasets.

Help us bring stories to the world! Join a global team of passionate gamers and contribute to delivering unforgettable game experiences.

For more information, visit .

description:

Location: (Remote)

USD 21.00 - 23.00 Per Hour

title: Client Service Associate
description:
Position Overview

The Client Service Associate supports Gatewood Wealth Solutions’ client service and operations functions by executing high-volume, detail-sensitive service requests with accuracy, timeliness, and professionalism. This role is responsible for preparing and processing account paperwork, coordinating custodial requests, monitoring follow-through, and ensuring that clients experience a smooth, organized, and high-touch service process.

The role is designed for someone who has strong client service instincts, comfort handling confidential financial information, and enough exposure to banking or financial account concepts to learn quickly. The ideal candidate may come from a bank teller, personal banker, retail banking, financial services support, or similar client-facing operations background where they have learned the basics of account ownership, registrations, documentation, and transaction accuracy without being overly experienced or set in another firm’s way of doing things.

Primary Responsibilities

Account Opening and Onboarding Support

· Prepare and process new account opening requests for individual, joint, trust, retirement, beneficiary, and other common account registrations.

· Review client-provided information for completeness and consistency before submitting paperwork or electronic signature packets.

· Coordinate with internal team members to confirm account type, titling, beneficiaries, funding instructions, and required supporting documentation.

· Track new account paperwork from preparation through signature, submission, approval, funding, and final confirmation.

· Communicate proactively with team members regarding missing information, paperwork status, expected timing, and next steps.

Move Money Transaction Requests

· Prepare and submit move money requests, including journals, ACH instructions, checks, wires, distributions, contributions, and other cash movement items as applicable.

· Confirm transaction details before submission, including account registration, account number, ownership, dollar amount, frequency, tax withholding requirements, and delivery instructions.

· Identify requests that require escalation, additional review, or advisor confirmation before processing.

· Maintain strong attention to risk controls, especially for retirement accounts, third-party instructions, beneficiary-related activity, and manual processing exceptions.

· Monitor transaction status through completion and provide timely updates to the appropriate internal team members.

Account Updates and Maintenance

· Process account maintenance requests, including beneficiary updates, title changes, address changes, contact information updates, trusted contact updates, and other client profile changes.

· Review maintenance requests for required forms, signatures, supporting documentation, and custodial requirements.

· Ensure client records remain accurate across applicable systems and notify team members when updates are complete.

· Recognize when an account update may create additional downstream tasks, such as changes to household records, portal access, billing setup, or reporting visibility.

Death Claims and Beneficiary Processing

· Support the preparation and tracking of death claim paperwork, beneficiary claim forms, inherited account opening paperwork, and related account transition documentation.

· Coordinate respectfully and carefully with internal team members during sensitive client family situations.

· Confirm required documentation such as death certificates, beneficiary information, entity documents, or custodial forms before submission.

· Monitor death claim and beneficiary processing status and escalate delays or documentation issues promptly.

ACATS and Asset Transfer Support

· Prepare and submit ACATS and other transfer paperwork for incoming assets.

· Review delivering firm statements to confirm account type, registration, ownership, approximate value, and potential transfer considerations.

· Track transfer status from submission through completion, including rejections, residual sweeps, transfer delays, and follow-up requirements.

· Coordinate with internal team members when transfer details do not align with the intended account setup or client onboarding plan.

Administrative Office Duties

· Front Desk and Phone coverage for the office as needed

· Client Check Deposits

· Ad hoc reporting and data management across CRM and various other technology platforms

Client Service and Communication Expectations

· Deliver a polished, responsive, and professional service experience in every internal and client-facing interaction.

· Communicate clearly, warmly, and accurately when requesting information, following up on paperwork, or providing status updates.

· Protect confidential client information and follow firm procedures for secure handling of sensitive data.

· Take ownership of assigned requests from start to finish rather than simply completing isolated tasks.

· Balance speed with accuracy, recognizing that attention to detail is critical in account registration, money movement, and beneficiary-related work.

Requirements

The ideal candidate is service-minded, coachable, organized, and detail-oriented. They may have previous experience as a bank teller, personal banker, branch associate, client service representative, operations assistant, or similar role where they were exposed to account types, client documentation, identity verification, transaction processing, and basic financial terminology.

This person should not need deep prior wealth management experience. Instead, Gatewood is seeking someone with a strong foundation in service, accuracy, follow-through, confidentiality, and professionalism who can be trained into the firm’s specific workflows, systems, language, and standards.

Required Qualifications

· Prior client service, banking, financial services, administrative operations, or comparable professional experience.

· Basic understanding of account ownership concepts, account registrations, beneficiary designations, or financial documentation preferred.

· Strong attention to detail and ability to review paperwork for completeness and consistency.

· Professional written and verbal communication skills.

· Demonstrated ability to manage multiple requests, deadlines, and follow-ups at the same time.

· Comfort handling confidential information and following documented procedures.

· Willingness to learn custodial systems, CRM workflows, electronic signature processes, and firm-specific operating standards.

Core Competencies

· Accuracy: Reviews names, account numbers, registrations, forms, and transaction details carefully before submission.

· Ownership: Follows each request through completion and communicates when items are delayed, rejected, or require clarification.

· Client Service: Brings patience, warmth, and professionalism to every client and internal team interaction.

· Coachability: Learns quickly, asks good questions, and applies feedback consistently.

· Process Discipline: Follows procedures, documents work clearly, and helps identify ways to improve repeatable workflows.

· Judgment: Knows when to pause, verify, and escalate rather than pushing a request forward with incomplete or conflicting information.

Systems and Tools

The Client Service Associate should be willing to learn and work within Gatewood’s operational technology environment, which may include custodial platforms, CRM workflows, electronic signature tools, client portal processes, document storage, Microsoft 365, and internal task management procedures.

Success Measures

· New account opening requests are prepared accurately and submitted in a timely manner.

· Move money requests are reviewed carefully, documented clearly, and processed with appropriate risk awareness.

· Account updates are completed with minimal rework and strong follow-through.

· ACATS and transfer requests are monitored consistently through completion.

· Death claim and beneficiary-related work is handled with care, accuracy, and appropriate urgency.

· Internal team members trust the associate to communicate clearly, identify issues early, and own the details from start to finish.

title: Senior IT Engineer & Technical Project Lead
description:
The Safe Group ontwerpt, integreert en beheert veiligheidstechnologie en ICT voor overheden, bedrijven en evenementen. Netwerken en IT-infrastructuur verbinden onze oplossingen: van camerabewaking en toegangscontrole tot communicatie, digital signage en tijdelijke installaties. Onze projecten lopen van vaste omgevingen tot festivals waar de deadline niet verschuift.

We zoeken een senior engineer die techniek en uitvoering bij elkaar brengt. Als ervaren collega binnen het IT-team neem je verantwoordelijkheid voor complexe technische oplossingen en trek je de uitvoering van toegewezen projecten waar geen aparte projectmanager nodig is.

Eerst in het veld, daarna helpen opschalen

Tijdens je eerste twee jaar neem je een actieve rol op in onze key projecten, waaronder ook festivals. Je ontwerpt, configureert, test en levert mee op. Je ziet op locatie hoe wij voorbereiden, beslissingen nemen, samenwerken en onder druk problemen oplossen. Zo bouw je inhoudelijke kennis én vertrouwen op bij klanten en collega’s.

Vanuit die praktijkervaring help je in de volgende fase het IT-team om technische werkwijzen, projectuitvoering, documentatie en kennisdeling over meer projecten heen te versterken. Je blijft dicht bij de technologie: verbeteringen moeten ook in het veld werken.

Wat je doet

Zelf ontwerpen, configureren en ondersteunen

  • Je vertaalt de vraag en verkochte scope naar een robuust technisch ontwerp en een uitvoerbare aanpak. Je bouwt en test zelf mee, van voorbereiding tot oplevering.
  • Je configureert en integreert systemen zoals camerabewaking, alarmsystemen, WiFi-netwerken, switches, routers, toegangscontrole en digital signage. Je troubleshoot zelf wanneer een systeem in de praktijk anders reageert dan op papier.
  • Je beheert en optimaliseert onze centrale firewall, VPN-concentrators en andere infrastructuur in het datacenter. Bij wijzigingen toets je de impact op beschikbaarheid, beveiliging, beheer en klanten.
  • Je ondersteunt klanten via telefoon en ticketsysteem, ook bij complexe technische vragen. Je escaleert wanneer nodig, onderzoekt de oorzaak en zorgt dat terugkerende problemen structureel worden opgelost.

Toegewezen projecten technisch leiden

  • Je maakt met het team een haalbare planning, verdeelt technisch werk en bewaakt afhankelijkheden, risico’s en mijlpalen.
  • Je bent voor je projecten een helder aanspreekpunt voor de klant en houdt interne collega’s tijdig op de hoogte.
  • Je signaleert scopewijzigingen, vertragingen en budget impact vroeg en stemt beslissingen af met de bevoegde collega’s.
  • Je bewaakt de kwaliteit van tests, documentatie en overdracht naar support en operations. Een project is pas klaar wanneer het beheer mee kan.

De werking sterker maken

  • Je deelt kennis, coacht collega’s inhoudelijk en maakt keuzes en oplossingen navolgbaar.
  • Je bespreekt terugkerende knelpunten uit projecten en support met het team en de IT Director, documenteert de oplossing en helpt verbeteringen in de praktijk brengen.
  • Je voert mee interne verbeterprojecten uit, zoals nieuwe hardware of software implementeren en systemen testen. Vanuit die ervaring help je de uitvoering schaalbaarder te maken zonder de voeling met klant en installatie te verliezen.

Je hebt al bewezen dat je complexe IT-omgevingen zelfstandig kunt doorgronden en realiseren. Je combineert technische diepgang met de rust en communicatie die nodig zijn om een team en een klant door een project te leiden.

Dit breng je mee

  • Sterke praktijkervaring met IP-netwerken: OSI laag 2 en 3, switching, routing, VLAN’s, firewalls, VPN’s, DHCP en DNS. Je begrijpt WiFi op systeem- én RF-niveau, ook voor grote client netwerken en draadloze point-to-point verbindingen.
  • Ervaring met Linux en Windows, pc- en server hardware, NAS-appliances en virtualisatie, bij voorkeur Proxmox. Je begrijpt de impact van een wijziging op een draaiende omgeving en kunt je werk waar zinvol met scripts ondersteunen.
  • Ervaring met het plannen en coördineren van technisch werk, inclusief heldere communicatie, documentatie en overdracht.
  • Een onderzoekende houding: je vindt oorzaken, weegt opties af en kunt je technische keuzes uitleggen.
  • Sterk Nederlands en professioneel Engels. Frans is een troef voor een deel van onze klanten en projecten.
  • Bereidheid om in je eerste jaren actief mee te werken op klantlocaties en festivals, met de pieken en deadlines die daarbij horen.

Hierin kun je bij ons groeien

Je bent in meerdere technische domeinen aantoonbaar hands-on en wilt je ook in nieuwe technologie verdiepen. Ervaring met camerabewaking, toegangscontrole, alarmen, digital signage, IoT, hosting, streaming video en audio of tijdelijke event infrastructuur is waardevol. Je hoeft ons volledige portfolio niet vooraf te beheersen, maar je neemt ook buiten je eigen specialisatie verantwoordelijkheid voor een werkend resultaat.

Hoe je werkt

Je neemt eigenaarschap, communiceert vroeg wanneer een plan moet wijzigen en houdt overzicht zonder het detail uit het oog te verliezen. Je steekt zelf de handen uit de mouwen, vraagt tijdig om een tweede blik en laat systemen en documentatie beter achter dan je ze aantrof.

title: Head of Payments
description:
Solance is building a tech-enabled payments company. We are here for businesses that operate across multiple entities, jurisdictions and currencies, and for sectors that traditional banks generally overlook. Think family offices, internationally operating companies, corporate service providers and the clients they serve. We are going through the final steps of the authorisation process with the Central Bank of Ireland, one of the most respected financial jurisdictions in Europe, and we are only getting started.

Payments and cards are not a feature of Solance. They are the foundation everything else stands on. Every client relationship, every product we layer on top, every promise we make to a family office or an entrepreneur, all of it runs on the rails, the ledger and the partnerships underneath. Today that foundation is assembled from a set of strong external providers, and it works. What we do not yet have is one person who owns the whole picture, independently, and who sets its direction from Solance's own logic rather than inheriting it from someone else's roadmap. That is the seat we are opening.

The role, in plain terms

You own Solance's payment rails and core platform strategy. Which rails we run on, which access model we use, which partners we build with, over what horizon and at what cost. You are the person who can sit in a vendor meeting and tell the difference between something that is genuinely hard and something that is merely inconvenient, and change the outcome because of it. You will not be building or operating the infrastructure with your own hands. You will be the one who understands it well enough to challenge everyone who does, and to make sure Solance is never quietly locked in.

Who we are looking for

You have ten years or more in payments, and most of that time has been on the banking and rails side, not in acquiring or merchant services. You have been accountable for real payment infrastructure in production, not just advised on it from the outside. You understand how the pieces actually fit together: ledger and account structures, settlement and reconciliation, scheme access and sponsorship, pre-funding and liquidity, ISO 20022, the real differences between core banking platforms. You do not need to configure any of it. You need to follow the design conversation and ask the one question that exposes a weak answer.

You have managed serious infrastructure suppliers, and you can point to a moment where you challenged a roadmap, a scope or a price and actually moved it. You build knowledge that outlasts you, the maps, the dependency registers, the vendor scorecards, rather than keeping it all in your own head. You have current, real relationships across sponsor banks, scheme operators and infrastructure providers, not a list of names you knew five years ago. You have worked inside a regulated institution, a bank, an EMI or a payment institution, and a supervisory relationship does not faze you. And you are equally credible in front of a board and in front of an engineering team. This role fails if you can only do one.

Above all, you are genuinely into payments. You know how money moves today, and you are honestly curious and hungry about where it goes next: direct participation, stablecoins, tokenisation, whatever is coming down the line. If payments are just a job to you rather than something you find genuinely interesting, this is not your seat.

Why this role exists

First, independence. Our payment capabilities today are built on a handful of excellent partners, each carefully chosen because of their own qualities. This means the deepest understanding of how our own product actually works sits with our suppliers rather than with us, and no one inside Solance owns the full picture. We want to change that, and we want you to be the reason it changes. When a partner declines, defers or prices high, Solance should be able to argue back on merit, and that starts with you.

Second, timing. A regulatory window is opening across Europe that, for the first time, makes direct participation in payment systems a real alternative to permanent indirect access through a sponsor bank. Whether Solance goes after that, on what timeline and at what cost, is one of the most important decisions we will take in the coming years, and it needs an owner who can frame it properly. That could be you.

Requirements

  • Ten years or more in payments, mostly on the banking and rails side.
  • Operator experience: accountable for payment infrastructure in production, not only advising on it.
  • Architectural literacy across rails, ledger, settlement, scheme access and core platforms, without needing to build it yourself.
  • A track record of challenging vendors on roadmap, scope and price, and winning.
  • Current, verifiable relationships across sponsor banks, scheme operators and infrastructure providers.
  • Time inside a regulated bank, EMI or payment institution, comfortable operating under supervision.
  • Credible with a board and with engineers in the same week.
  • A real passion for payments, both how they work now and where they are heading.

What is in it for you

You report straight to the CEO, not three layers down, and you own one of the most important mandates in the company. You get to set the direction of Solance's entire payments foundation at exactly the moment the market is being reshaped by new regulation, and you get to do it without the drag of a large organisation sitting above you. This comes with a competitive package and the rare chance to put your name on the infrastructure of a bank being built the right way, from the ground up. It is a builder's seat, not a caretaker's.

Where you are based

This is a Dublin role, and we mean it. We want you here, with the team, because the job only works if you are close to the people building the product and in the room when the decisions get made. You will also be on the road often, in front of sponsor banks, scheme operators and industry bodies, because that is where the relationships that matter actually live. So, in plain terms: based in Dublin, travelling regularly, not remote. If you are not willing to be here with us, this is not your role.

Let us talk

If this reads like you, get in touch. And if it reads like someone you rate, send them our way, or send us the introduction. The best people in this world almost always come recommended, so a good word from you carries weight.

title: Systems Engineer
description:
Jobbeskrivning

Would you like to work with advanced technology combining sensors, hardware, and software in safety-critical systems? We are currently looking for a Senior Systems Engineer to join an innovative technology company in Lund.



About the role

As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will play a central and leading role in developing advanced sensor systems and technical solutions with high requirements for performance, reliability, and safety. You will take a system-level perspective and ensure that hardware, software, sensors, and other subsystems work together effectively within the complete product.

You will collaborate closely with specialists in software, electronics, mechanics, optics, and testing. The role requires someone who can create structure, establish a clear technical direction, and lead cross-functional engineering activities from initial concept to a functioning and verified solution.

Your responsibilities may include:

Developing and maintaining system architectures
Defining, analyzing, and breaking down system requirements
Ensuring traceability between requirements, design, implementation, and verification
Leading and coordinating technical activities across engineering disciplines
Coordinating interfaces between hardware, software, sensors, and external systems
Planning and supporting system integration, verification, and validation
Performing technical risk assessments and system performance analyses
Collaborating with internal teams, external partners, customers, and suppliers
Communicating technical decisions and creating alignment between stakeholders
Providing technical leadership and guidance to development teams and project management



Baskunskaper

We are looking for someone who has:

A relevant Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering
Several years of experience in systems engineering or complex product development
Experience in requirements management, system architecture, and technical documentation
A strong understanding of hardware and software interaction
Experience in system integration, verification, and validation
Experience leading technical activities or cross-functional engineering teams
The ability to approach complex technical challenges in a structured manner
Excellent communication skills in Swedish and English

Experience in the following areas is considered an advantage:

The automotive industry, particularly ADAS, autonomous systems, or active safety systems
Sensor-based systems, computer vision, optics, radar, lidar, or camera technology
Functional safety and standards such as ISO 26262
Model-based systems engineering and requirements management tools
The Swedish Armed Forces, defence industry, or another safety-critical and regulated environment
Product development from early concepts and prototypes through testing and industrialization



Personliga färdigheter, egenskaper, erfarenhet

Your personal qualities are essential for succeeding in this role. We are looking for someone with a strong inner drive who takes initiative, creates momentum, and ensures that technical activities move forward. You are comfortable taking ownership and making decisions, even when the available information is incomplete or the technical challenges are complex.



You are highly communicative and able to explain complicated technical matters clearly and confidently to different audiences. You naturally build relationships and create trust with colleagues, customers, suppliers, and other stakeholders.



As a social and collaborative person, you enjoy bringing people together and creating engagement around common goals. You listen to others, welcome different perspectives, and can challenge ideas constructively when needed.



You also have the ability and confidence to lead. This does not necessarily mean formal personnel responsibility, but you should be comfortable setting direction, coordinating others, following up on progress, and helping teams make decisions. You lead through clarity, credibility, and engagement.

You combine these qualities with an analytical and solution-oriented mindset. You are pragmatic, hands-on, and motivated by turning ideas and requirements into functioning, verified products.



Vi erbjuder

ou will join an innovative and technology-intensive environment where you can work closely with both the product and some of the industry’s most exciting technologies. You will have the opportunity to influence technical direction, lead cross-functional activities, and contribute to the development of solutions with a clear safety purpose.





Location: Lund

title: Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
description:
Position Overview

This is a global role. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Counsel, Contracts & Compliance serves as a core legal resource supporting IP House’s commercial contracting, regulatory compliance, and legal operations functions worldwide, working alongside the Counsel, IP Litigation & Enforcement and the wider legal team.

The role offers an excellent opportunity for an early-career lawyer to gain hands-on experience supporting a high-growth, global organization, with a focus on commercial contracts, legal compliance, and internal governance. In a given week, Counsel may negotiate a client MSA or vendor agreement, help refine a compliance training module, support a proposal or RFP response, and liaise with external counsel in the US, UK, or another jurisdiction. The role works cross-functionally with Client Success, Client Solutions, Operations, and Finance teams to ensure operational integrity and mitigate legal risk, and suits a detail-oriented self-starter who is commercially minded, highly organized, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

Commercial Contracts

• Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial contracts, including client master service agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), vendor and partnership agreements, NDAs, and licensing and procurement agreements.

• Own contract lifecycle management, including tracking key terms, obligations, deadlines, and renewals across the contract portfolio.

• Support the proposal and RFP process with timely input on contractual terms and risk-related matters.

Compliance & Legal Risk

• Assist with the implementation and monitoring of internal policies on data privacy, anti-bribery, competition, and third-party risk.

• Conduct periodic audits and reviews to support compliance with global standards, including GDPR, CCPA, the UK Bribery Act, and the FCPA.

• Develop, refine, and deliver internal training materials and compliance documentation for the business.

Legal Operations & Governance

• Conduct legal research and provide support on ad hoc matters, including corporate filings and IP-related issues.

• Liaise with external counsel in the US, UK, and other jurisdictions on compliance and contract-related matters.

• Maintain and organize legal templates, playbooks, and knowledge management tools, and help drive adoption of legal AI tools to improve turnaround times and consistency across the team.

• Partner with the COO and the Counsel, IP Litigation & Enforcement to help execute and enforce IP House’s legal compliance requirements and standards across the business.

Qualifications

Required

• Juris Doctor (JD) with admission to a United States bar, or a UK law degree (LLB) with completion of the solicitor (or barrister) qualification and admission or entitlement to practice in England & Wales or another UK jurisdiction.

• 2+ years of post-qualification experience (PQE) gained in a law firm or in-house legal environment.

• Strong drafting and negotiation skills, particularly in commercial agreements.

• Familiarity with regulatory compliance topics such as data privacy, anti-bribery, or competition law.

• Experience in legal research, project coordination, and cross-functional collaboration.

• Based in, and holding the unrestricted right to work in, the United States or the United Kingdom.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, a commercially savvy and risk-aware mindset, and strong attention to detail in a fast-paced, dynamic global environment.

Highly Desired

• Experience using legal AI tools to improve efficiency, consistency, and turnaround time.

• Experience working with contracts in the IP enforcement or content and brand protection industry.

Desired

• Additional language capability beyond English.

• Prior experience in a fast-paced, multi-jurisdictional services environment.

Location, Travel & Working Pattern

This role is open to candidates based anywhere in the United States or the United Kingdom, working fully remotely or on a hybrid basis from one of our offices, depending on location. Some flexibility in working hours is expected to accommodate colleagues and clients in other time zones. Occasional domestic or international travel may be required.

Why Join IP House?

• Global Mission — help the world’s top brands protect their most valuable assets across every major market.

• Early Impact — join a growing legal team where your work has immediate visibility and value, partnering with colleagues across the globe.

• Learning Environment — work closely with seasoned attorneys and business leaders to grow your legal and commercial skills.

• Flexible Environment — remote or hybrid options depending on location, with global collaboration across five continents.

• High Growth, High Impact — be part of a fast-scaling organization with a strong reputation for results — and room to grow with it.

Compensation

Salary Range: $100,000–$125,000 USD per year (United States) or £65,000–£75,000 GBP per year (United Kingdom), plus bonus

Classification: Full-time, permanent (exempt where applicable)

Base salary is dependent on the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience, and is benchmarked to the market in which they are based. Base salary and bonus are supplemented by a comprehensive local benefits package.

Equal Opportunity

IP House seeks excellence through diversity in its staff. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion or belief, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, veteran status, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are happy to discuss reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process.

title: Operations Controller, EMEA
description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

The opportunity:

As part of the EMEA Accounting team in Amsterdam, we are opening a role for an Operations Controller – a hands-on leader for accounting, control, and finance automation across 15+ countries. This is an opportunity to build modern finance operations in a fast-growing multinational environment, as part of a team that is shaping and learning from the new world of autonomous finance firsthand; a genuinely unique opportunity to get ahead of the market. The role requires a strong grasp of financial reporting and VAT principles, sharp analytical thinking, and the professional judgment needed to lead across stakeholders and time zones under pressure.

You will:

  • Own full monthly close timeliness, completeness and accuracy across a growing multi-entity footprint, overseeing standardized schedules and checklists that scale as entity count grows.
  • Own accuracy of local Revenue and COGS, including transfer pricing calculations based on approved methodology.
  • Control cost, balance sheet and liquidity through among others OPEX and T&E challenge, financial anomaly investigation, deposits and cash flow review.
  • Build and deliver automation roadmap for the Accounting function within and outside the ERP by identifying manual, repeatable work and sequencing its removal.
  • Enforce correct output and input VAT recording end-to-end, based on strong technical acumen on EU and international VAT principles.
  • Drive corrective actions across internal and external stakeholders to enforce correct financial and VAT accountingImplement e-invoicing readiness for local continuous transaction control mandates.
  • Partnership with Business to capture new commercial models and contract structures before they hit the ledger, embedding them into standard accounting workflows; with FP&A to sharpen figures and inputs feeding their reporting models; and with other back office functions (Legal, People, Workplace) on recurring compliance, bookings, and ad hoc initiatives.
  • Provide leadership through supervising and developing the Accounting team.

You should have:

  • 5+ years of progressive accounting and operational finance experience in a high-growth company.
  • Experience working in a multinational setting with cross-border reporting needs.
  • Strong background in GAAP, financial reporting and ERP systems.
  • Proven experience with applying VAT rules and VAT accounting across Europe.
  • Top level proficiency in deploying and overseeing automated finance tools, agent frameworks and modern financial data stacks.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to coordinate across departments and manage external relationships.
  • Exceptional organizational, prioritization and planning skills, and keen attention to detail.

What is in it for you:

  • An opportunity to contribute to one of the fastest-growing companies, where you’ll have the chance to create a global impact while being a part of a thriving multinational environment.

  • Commute expenses: Flexport will cover home-office commuting costs for employees living outside of Amsterdam.
  • Amazing office in the heart of Amsterdam.
  • 25 working days as vacation days based on full time employment.
  • Health insurance: Flexport offers a collective health insurance plan including a basic package and any available additional packages. Your monthly premium is fully paid by Flexport.
  • A defined pension contribution scheme.
  • Equity program: every team member becomes a shareholder, aligning our success with yours. As a private company in a multi-trillion dollar industry, you have a direct stake in our collective growth and success.
  • Employee Assistance Program through Aetna Resources for Living: Flexport provides an employer-sponsored program at no cost to you and your household members.
  • Parental leave benefit: Flexport is here to support you and your families in one of the most important times in life – the birth of a child! Our parental leave program allows both mothers and partners to take time off from work for pregnancy, childbirth, and to bond with your new child.

title: Solution Architect, Professional Services
description:
About Ottimate

Ottimate is a leading provider of AI-powered automation solutions that help businesses streamline financial operations, optimize procurement, and manage spend with ease. Our platform integrates seamlessly with ERP, accounting, and procurement systems, enabling organizations to work smarter and scale efficiently.

About the Role

As a Solution Architect at Ottimate, you are the primary owner of the technical scoping process for new customer engagements. This role exists at the intersection of sales and professional services: you ensure that every Statement of Work reflects an accurate, well-scoped solution before a customer signs, and that the implementation team inherits a clear, executable plan when they do.

This role was created in response to a deliberate strategic shift: the Sales Engineering team is moving away from SOW authorship to focus on demonstrations and ICP deal acceleration. That work now belongs to you. You will own the scoping conversation for complex and custom deals, serve as the technical authority in pre-implementation discussions, and build the scoping process infrastructure that allows Ottimate to take on more sophisticated implementations with confidence.

The right person for this role combines deep AP and ERP knowledge with the consultative instinct to run a discovery conversation and the precision to translate what they hear into a scoped and defensible SOW. You are not primarily an architect in the engineering sense - you are a technical scoping authority who understands how Ottimate works at depth and can map that to what a customer actually needs.

Key Responsibilities

Scoping and SOW ownership

  • Own the end-to-end scoping process for complex, custom, and non-ICP deals - from initial discovery through SOW finalization and internal approval
  • Lead technical discovery sessions with prospects, translating business requirements, ERP configurations, and AP workflows into a clear, accurate scope
  • Author and validate SOWs for all custom work, including integration requirements, configuration complexity, data migration needs, and estimated effort in coordination with Product and Engineering
  • Present SOW components on the weekly SOW review call with Product and Engineering, incorporating feedback and ensuring technical sign-off before commercial handoff
  • Maintain and improve SOW templates, scoping frameworks, and discovery question banks that make the scoping process faster and more consistent over time

Technical authority and pre-implementation partnership

  • Serve as the most credible technical voice in pre-implementation customer conversations - able to speak with authority on ERP integration behavior, PO matching logic, Item Validation configuration, and AP workflow design
  • Define the handoff standard between scoping and delivery: ensure the PS and Implementation teams inherit engagements with complete documentation, clear scope boundaries, and no outstanding technical ambiguity
  • Partner with the Strategic Consultant on existing customer expansions where scoping complexity warrants SA involvement
  • Support the SE team on ICP deals when technical questions exceed standard demo depth - providing scoping input without owning the full SE motion

Process and infrastructure development

  • Refine and own the scoping process as a function - not just as a set of individual deals, but as a repeatable, documented capability that scales as deal volume and complexity increase
  • Define rules of engagement with the SE team on when and how scoping handoffs occur, in partnership with the CSO's direction on SE bandwidth allocation
  • Develop internal reference materials - integration guides, configuration decision trees, ERP-specific scoping notes - that reduce reliance on tribal knowledge
  • Track scoping accuracy over time: compare scoped estimates to actual delivery hours and use variance data to improve future scoping precision

Cross-functional collaboration

  • Partner closely with the SE team to ensure clean, timely handoffs on deals that require custom scoping - being responsive to sales timelines without compromising scoping quality
  • Work with Product and Engineering on JIRA ticket creation and hour estimation for custom work, ensuring approved scope is accurately reflected before contracts are signed
  • Collaborate with the Director of PS on org-wide scoping strategy, capacity planning for complex deals, and the evolution of the SA function as the business scales
  • Contribute product and integration intelligence back to the team - patterns in what customers ask for, where scoping breaks down, and where product gaps create delivery risk



Requirements

Experience

  • 6+ years in solution architecture, technical pre-sales, implementation consulting, or a senior professional services role within a B2B SaaS environment
  • Deep, hands-on experience with ERP and accounting system integrations - NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Acumatica, Microsoft Business Central, or QuickBooks Online
  • Demonstrated experience authoring SOWs for complex software implementations, including integration scope, configuration requirements, and effort estimation
  • Strong working knowledge of AP workflows: PO matching methodologies, invoice processing logic, payment infrastructure, and discrepancy resolution
  • Experience operating at the boundary between sales and professional services - you understand what it means to scope something that someone else has to build

Skills and qualities

  • Technical depth without technical arrogance - you can go deep on integration architecture and also explain it clearly to a CFO
  • Precision in language and documentation - your SOWs do not leave room for misinterpretation, and your discovery notes are something an implementation team can actually use
  • Consultative and curious in discovery - you ask better questions than the customer expects, and you listen for what they are not saying as much as what they are
  • Accountable to accuracy - you treat a scoping miss as a personal failure, not an acceptable variance, and you build process to prevent the next one
  • Collaborative with sales and implementation - you understand the pressure on both sides and operate as a trusted bridge, not a bottleneck

Benefits

We care deeply about making Ottimate an incredible place to work and invest a significant amount of time and energy into creating and maintaining a company culture that provides our team with a generous level of support whilst inspiring them to do their best work.

The specific benefits/perks we offer are continually evolving, but currently include:

  • Compensation: $130,000-150,000 per year + bonus compensation.
  • Medical, Dental, Vision and other Company-Subsidized Benefits for you and your family.
  • Employer-sponsored 401(k) with company match.
  • Paid Time Off (and the encouragement to use it).
  • Promote from within philosophy.

Beyond the tangible benefits though:

  • You will be part of a growing team, at a pinnacle moment of scale for the business and experience the excitement of working in a startup where each action makes a huge difference.
  • You will have the agency to solve difficult problems creatively, the freedom to explore work that inspires you, and infrastructure to ensure you're constantly challenged and developing.
  • You will work with sharp, passionate teammates solving some of the most unique challenges and positioning our product as a premier finance automation solution.
  • Our commitment to empowering a diverse and inclusive workforce, celebrating differences, and creating a safe space for our employees to bring their whole selves to work is second to note.
  • We are transforming entire industries using innovative technology including Artificial Intelligence, Payment Tech, and Neural Networks.
  • Our leaders lead with a people-first approach; inspiring excellence, nurturing ideas, and finding creative ways to eliminate obstacles for cultivating growth.
  • We truly love what we do and who we do it with - and we think you will too!

Ottimate is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or marital status. If you are excited about the role but do not meet 100% of the qualifications listed above, we encourage you to apply. Nothing in this job posting should be construed as an offer or guarantee of employment.

title: Project Manager - Infrastructure- Kingston, Surrey - £70,000
